title.raw: 卷13 皇后列傳 Volume 13: Bigraphies of Empresses

sentences.zh: 漢因秦制，帝之祖母曰太皇太后，母曰皇太后，妃曰皇后，餘則多稱夫人，隨世增損，非如周禮有夫人、嬪婦、御妻之定數焉。

translations.literal: The Han followed Qin institutions: the emperor's paternal grandmother was styled Grand Empress Dowager, his mother Empress Dowager, his principal consort Empress; the rest were mostly called Lady, increased or reduced with the age—not like the Rites of Zhou with fixed numbers of ladies, concubines, wives, and palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, who took over Qin practice, the emperor's grandmother was Grand Empress Dowager, his mother Empress Dowager, and his chief consort Empress; everyone else was usually called Lady, with titles shifting over time rather than the fixed ranks of lady, concubine, wife, and palace woman set out in the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 魏晉相因，時有昇降，前史言之具矣。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin carried this on, with promotions and demotions from time to time; earlier histories have set it out fully.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin inherited the same system, raising and lowering ranks as times changed; earlier histories already tell that story in full.

sentences.zh: 魏氏王業之兆雖始於神元，至於昭成之前，世崇儉質，妃嬙嬪御，率多闕焉，惟以次第為稱。

translations.literal: Though the omen of Wei royal enterprise began with Shenyuan, down to before Emperor Zhaocheng the age prized austerity; consorts, concubines, and palace women were mostly lacking, and only order of precedence served as title.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei kings' mandate may have begun with Shenyuan, but until the reign before Emperor Zhaocheng the court prized plain living: few consorts or palace women are recorded, and women were known only by their rank in the sequence.

sentences.zh: 而章、平、思、昭、穆、惠、煬、烈八帝，妃后無聞。

translations.literal: Yet for the eight rulers Emperor Zhang, Emperor Ping, Emperor Si, Emperor Zhao, Emperor Mu, Emperor Hui, Emperor Yang, and Emperor Lie, no empress or consort is heard of.
translations.idiomatic: For eight early rulers—Zhang, Ping, Si, Zhao, Mu, Hui, Yang, and Lie—no empress or consort is named at all.

sentences.zh: 太祖追尊祖妣，皆從帝諡為皇后，始立中宮，餘妾或稱夫人，多少無限，然皆有品次。

translations.literal: Taizu posthumously honored his forebears' wives, all taking the emperor's posthumous title as empress; the central palace was first established; other women might be called Lady, without limit in number, yet all had grades.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu raised his ancestors' wives to empress in posthumous title, established the central palace, and allowed other women the title Lady in unlimited number, each with a defined rank.

sentences.zh: 世祖稍增左右昭儀及貴人、椒房、中式數等，後庭漸已多矣。

translations.literal: Shizu gradually added Left and Right Worthy Ladies, Honored Persons, Pepper Chamber, Central Style, and several other ranks; the rear palace grew numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu gradually added left and right worthy ladies, honored persons, pepper-chamber attendants, central-style ranks, and the like, and the rear palace swelled.

sentences.zh: 又魏故事，將立皇后必令手鑄金人，以成者為吉，不成則不得立也。

translations.literal: By Wei precedent, before establishing an empress she had to cast a golden figure by hand; success was auspicious, failure meant she could not be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Wei custom required a woman to cast a gold figure with her own hands before she could be made empress: success meant good fortune; failure barred the throne.

sentences.zh: 又世祖、高宗緣保母劬勞之恩，並極尊崇之義，雖事乖典禮，而觀過知仁。

translations.literal: Again, Shizu and Gaozong, moved by wet-nurses' toil and care, both showed the utmost honor—though the acts breached ritual, one may see benevolence through the fault.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu and Gaozong both lavished honor on their wet-nurses out of gratitude for exhausting care; the practice broke ritual, yet the kindness behind the breach is plain.

sentences.zh: 高祖改定內官，左右昭儀位視大司馬，三夫人視三公，三嬪視三卿，六嬪視六卿，世婦視中大夫，御女視元士。

translations.literal: Gaozu reformed the inner offices: Left and Right Worthy Ladies ranked with the Grand Marshal; Three Ladies with the Three Excellencies; Three Consorts with the three ministers; Six Consorts with the six ministers; World Wives with palace grand masters; Palace Women with chief clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu reorganized the inner court: left and right worthy ladies equaled the grand marshal; three ladies the three excellencies; three consorts the three ministers; six consorts the six ministers; world wives palace grand masters; palace women chief clerks.

sentences.zh: 後置女職，以典內事。

translations.literal: Later female offices were added to administer inner affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he added female offices to run palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 內司視尚書令、僕。

translations.literal: The Inner Director ranked with the Directors of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: The inner director ranked with the directors of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 作司、大監、女侍中三官視二品。

translations.literal: The Director of Works, Grand Supervisor, and Female Palace Attendant—the three offices—ranked at the second grade.
translations.idiomatic: Director of works, grand supervisor, and female palace attendant—the three posts—held second-grade rank.

sentences.zh: 監，女尚書，美人，女史、女賢人、書史、書女、小書女五官，視三品。

translations.literal: Supervisor, Female Master of Writing, Beauty, Female Scribe, Female Worthy, Book Scribe, Book Woman, and Junior Book Woman—the five offices—ranked at the third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor, female master of writing, beauty, female scribe, female worthy, book scribe, book woman, and junior book woman—five offices—held third-grade rank.

sentences.zh: 中才人、供人、中使女生、才人、恭使宮人視四品，春衣、女酒、女饗、女食、奚官女奴視五品。

translations.literal: Central Talented Woman, Attendant, Central Palace Maid, Talented Woman, and Respectful Palace Woman ranked at the fourth grade; Spring Robe, Wine Woman, Feast Woman, Food Woman, and Palace Slave ranked at the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Central talented woman, attendant, central palace maid, talented woman, and respectful palace woman were fourth grade; spring robe, wine woman, feast woman, food woman, and palace slave were fifth.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 神元皇后竇氏，沒鹿回部大人賓之女也。

translations.literal: Empress of Shenyuan, Lady Dou, was daughter of Bin, paramount chief of the Moluhui tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Empress of Shenyuan, née Dou, was the daughter of Bin, paramount chief of the Moluhui tribe.

sentences.zh: 賓臨終，誡其二子速侯、回題，令善事帝。

translations.literal: As Bin lay dying he admonished his two sons Suho and Huiti to serve the emperor well.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Bin warned his sons Suho and Huiti to serve the emperor faithfully.

sentences.zh: 及賓卒，速侯等欲因帝會喪為變，語頗漏泄，帝聞之，知其終不奉順，乃先圖之。

translations.literal: When Bin died, Suho and the others wished to use the emperor's attendance at the funeral to raise a revolt; word leaked somewhat; the emperor heard and, knowing they would never submit, moved against them first.
translations.idiomatic: After Bin's death Suho and his brothers planned a coup when the emperor came to the funeral; word leaked; the emperor knew they would never submit and struck first.

sentences.zh: 於是伏勇士於宮中，晨起以佩刀殺后，馳使告速侯等，言后暴崩。

translations.literal: He then hid warriors in the palace; at dawn he killed the empress with his belt knife, sent a fast rider to tell Suho and the rest that the empress had died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Warriors lay hidden in the palace; at dawn the emperor killed the empress with his belt knife and sent riders to Suho saying she had died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 速侯等驚走來赴，因執而殺之。

translations.literal: Suho and the others, alarmed, rushed to attend; he seized and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Suho and his brothers ran to the palace in alarm and were seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 文帝皇后封氏，生桓、穆二帝，早崩。

translations.literal: Empress of Emperor Wen, Lady Feng, bore Emperors Huan and Mu and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's empress, née Feng, bore Emperors Huan and Mu and died young.

sentences.zh: 桓帝立，乃葬焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huan took the throne she was buried.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huan was enthroned, she was buried at last.

sentences.zh: [3]高宗初，穿天淵池，獲一石銘，稱桓帝葬母封氏，遠近赴會二十餘萬人。

translations.literal: [3] Early in Gaozong's reign, while digging the Tianyuan Pool, a stone inscription was found saying Emperor Huan buried his mother Lady Feng; more than two hundred thousand came from near and far to the gathering.
translations.idiomatic: [3] Early in Gaozong's reign workers digging the Tianyuan Pool found a stone inscription recording that Emperor Huan buried his mother Lady Feng; more than two hundred thousand people gathered from near and far.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，命藏之太廟。

translations.literal: The responsible offices reported; he ordered it stored in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The court reported the find; the emperor ordered the stone kept in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 次妃蘭氏，生二子，長子曰藍，早卒；

translations.literal: The next consort, Lady Lan, bore two sons; the elder was called Lan and died young;
translations.idiomatic: A secondary consort, Lady Lan, bore two sons; the elder, named Lan, died young;

sentences.zh: 次子，思帝也。

translations.literal: the younger was Emperor Si.
translations.idiomatic: the younger became Emperor Si.

sentences.zh: 桓帝皇后祁氏，[4]生三子，長曰普根，次惠帝，次煬帝。

translations.literal: Empress of Emperor Huan, Lady Qi, [4] bore three sons: the eldest Pugen, next Emperor Hui, next Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan's empress, née Qi, [4] bore three sons: Pugen the eldest, then Emperor Hui, then Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 平文崩，后攝國事，時人謂之女國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Pingwen died the empress held state affairs; people called it a women's realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Pingwen died the empress governed; people spoke of a women's state.

sentences.zh: 后性猛忌，平文之崩，后所為也。

translations.literal: The empress was fierce and jealous; Emperor Pingwen's death was her doing.
translations.idiomatic: She was fierce and jealous; Emperor Pingwen's death was her work.

sentences.zh: 平文皇后王氏，廣寧人也。

translations.literal: Empress of Emperor Pingwen, Lady Wang, was a native of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Pingwen's empress, née Wang, came from Guangning.

sentences.zh: 年十三，因事入宮，得幸於平文，生昭成帝。

translations.literal: At thirteen she entered the palace on business and won Emperor Pingwen's favor, bearing Emperor Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen she entered the palace on an errand, won Emperor Pingwen's favor, and bore Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 平文崩，昭成在襁褓。

translations.literal: When Emperor Pingwen died, Zhaocheng was still in swaddling clothes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Pingwen died, Zhaocheng was still an infant in swaddling clothes.

sentences.zh: 時國有內難，將害諸皇子。

translations.literal: The state then had internal strife and men meant to kill the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Civil strife broke out; plotters meant to kill the princes.

sentences.zh: 后匿帝於袴中，懼人知，呪曰：「若天祚未終者，汝便無聲。

translations.literal: The empress hid the emperor in her trousers, fearing discovery, and prayed: "If Heaven's mandate is not ended, be silent.
translations.idiomatic: She hid the child in her trousers and prayed, fearing discovery: "If Heaven's mandate is not ended, be silent."

sentences.zh: 」遂良久不啼，得免於難。

translations.literal: " For a long time he did not cry and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: " He did not cry for a long time and was spared.

sentences.zh: 昭成初欲定都於灅源川，築城郭，起宮室，議不決。

translations.literal: When Zhaocheng first wished to fix the capital at the Luanyuan River, build walls, and raise palaces, deliberation did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaocheng first planned to settle on the Luanyuan River, build walls, and raise palaces, the court could not agree.

sentences.zh: 后聞之，曰：「國自上世，遷徙為業。

translations.literal: The empress heard and said: "From high antiquity our state has made migration its calling.
translations.idiomatic: The empress objected: "From antiquity this people has lived by migration.

sentences.zh: 今事難之後，基業未固。

translations.literal: Now, after hardship, the foundation is not firm.
translations.idiomatic: After recent troubles the foundation is still weak.

sentences.zh: 若城郭而居，一旦寇來，難卒遷動。

translations.literal: If we dwell within walls, when raiders come we cannot move at once.
translations.idiomatic: If we build walled towns and enemies strike, we cannot flee at once."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: He stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 烈帝之崩，國祚殆危，興復大業，后之力也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lie died the throne was nearly lost; the great revival was her work.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lie died the dynasty nearly perished; she did the work of revival.

sentences.zh: 十八年崩，葬雲中金陵。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year she died and was buried at Jinling in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the eighteenth year and was buried at Jinling in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne she was paired in sacrifice at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne she received paired sacrifice in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 獻明皇后賀氏，父野干，東部大人。

translations.literal: Empress Xianming, Lady He, had as father Yegan, paramount chief of the Eastern Division.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xianming, née He—her father Yegan was paramount chief of the Eastern Division.

sentences.zh: 后少以容儀選入東宮，生太祖。

translations.literal: The empress in youth was chosen into the Eastern Palace for beauty and bore Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen young into the eastern palace for her looks, she bore Taizu.

sentences.zh: 苻洛之內侮也，后與太祖及故臣吏避難北徙。

translations.literal: When Fu Luo raided within the borders, the empress fled north with Taizu and former ministers and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Luo invaded, she fled north with Taizu and loyal officials.

sentences.zh: 俄而，高車奄來抄掠，后乘車與太祖避賊而南。

translations.literal: Soon the Gaoche came raiding; the empress rode in a cart with Taizu fleeing south from the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gaoche raiders struck; she rode south with Taizu to escape them.

sentences.zh: 中路失轄，后懼，仰天而告曰：「國家胤冑，豈止爾絕滅也！

translations.literal: Midway the axle broke; the empress in fear looked to Heaven and said: "The imperial line—can it end with us alone!
translations.idiomatic: Midway the axle broke. She looked up in terror and cried: "Can the imperial line end with us alone!

sentences.zh: 惟神靈扶助。

translations.literal: Only let the spirits aid us.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits, aid us!"

sentences.zh: 」遂馳，輪正不傾。

translations.literal: They galloped on; the wheel held straight and did not tip.
translations.idiomatic: They galloped on; the wheel held true and did not tip.

sentences.zh: 行百餘里，至七介山南而得免難。

translations.literal: After more than a hundred li they reached the south of Mount Qijie and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a hundred li they reached the south slope of Mount Qijie and were safe.

sentences.zh: 後劉顯使人將害太祖，帝姑為顯弟亢埿妻，知之，密以告后，梁眷亦來告難。

translations.literal: Later Liu Xian sent men to kill Taizu; the emperor's aunt was wife to Xian's brother Kangnuili and knew; she secretly told the empress; Liang Juan also came to warn of danger.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Xian sent men to kill Taizu. The emperor's aunt, married to Xian's brother Kangnuili, learned of it and warned the empress in secret; Liang Juan brought the same warning.

sentences.zh: 后乃令太祖去之。

translations.literal: The empress then had Taizu leave.
translations.idiomatic: She sent Taizu away at once.

sentences.zh: 后夜飲顯使醉。

translations.literal: At night the empress made Xian's envoy drunk.
translations.idiomatic: That night she plied Xian's envoy with wine until he was drunk.

sentences.zh: 向晨，故驚厩中羣馬，顯使起視馬。

translations.literal: Toward dawn she deliberately startled the stable horses; the envoy rose to look at the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn she stampeded the stable horses; the envoy rose to inspect them.

sentences.zh: 后泣而謂曰：「吾諸子始皆在此，今盡亡失。

translations.literal: The empress wept and said: "All my sons were here; now they are all gone.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, she said: "All my sons were here; now they have vanished.

sentences.zh: 汝等誰殺之？

translations.literal: Which of you killed them?
translations.idiomatic: Which of you killed them?"

sentences.zh: 」故顯不使急追。

translations.literal: Thus Xian's men did not pursue in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's men did not pursue in haste.

sentences.zh: [5]太祖得至賀蘭部，羣情未甚歸附，后從弟外朝大人悅，舉部隨從，供奉盡禮。

translations.literal: [5] Taizu reached the Helan tribe; the people's hearts had not yet fully turned to him; the empress's cousin Yue, outer-court grandee, led his whole tribe to follow and served with full ritual.
translations.idiomatic: [5] When Taizu reached the Helan tribe hearts were not yet won; the empress's cousin Yue, an outer-court grandee, led his whole tribe to follow and served with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 顯怒，將害后，后夜奔亢埿家，匿神車中三日，亢埿舉室請救，乃得免。

translations.literal: Xian was enraged and meant to kill the empress; she fled by night to Kangnuili's house and hid three days in the spirit cart; Kangnuili's whole household begged for her life and she was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xian raged and meant to kill her; she fled by night to Kangnuili's house and hid three days in the spirit cart until his household begged for her life.

sentences.zh: 會劉顯部亂，始得亡歸。

translations.literal: When Liu Xian's tribe fell into disorder she at last escaped home.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xian's tribe fell into disorder she escaped home at last.

sentences.zh: 後后弟染干忌太祖之得人心，舉兵圍逼行宮，后出謂染干曰：「汝等今安所置我，而欲殺吾子也？

translations.literal: Later the empress's brother Ran'gan, jealous that Taizu had won hearts, raised troops and besieged the traveling palace; the empress came out and said to Ran'gan: "Where will you place me now, yet you mean to kill my son?
translations.idiomatic: Later her brother Ran'gan, jealous of Taizu's popularity, besieged the traveling palace. The empress confronted him: "Where will you put me, if you kill my son?"

sentences.zh: 」染干慚而去。

translations.literal: Ran'gan left in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ran'gan withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 道武皇后慕容氏，寶之季女也。

translations.literal: Empress of Emperor Daowu, Lady Murong, was the youngest daughter of Murong Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu's empress, née Murong, was Murong Bao's youngest daughter.

sentences.zh: 中山平，入充掖庭，得幸。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was pacified she entered the rear palace and won favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongshan fell she entered the rear palace and won favor.

sentences.zh: 左丞相衞王儀等奏請立皇后，帝從羣臣議，令后鑄金人，成，乃立之，告於郊廟。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Prince Wei of the Guard and others memorialized to establish an empress; the emperor followed the ministers' counsel, ordered the empress to cast a golden figure; it succeeded and she was enthroned, with announcement at the suburban altars.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei of the Guard, left chancellor, and others asked that she be made empress. The emperor agreed, had her cast the gold figure; it succeeded, and she was enthroned with rites at the suburban altars.

sentences.zh: 封后母孟為漂陽君。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed the empress's mother Lady Meng as Lady of Piaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed her mother Lady Meng as Lady of Piaoyang.

translations.literal: [6] Later she died.
translations.idiomatic: [6] She died later.

sentences.zh: 道武宣穆皇后劉氏，劉眷女也。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanmu of Emperor Daowu, Lady Liu, was daughter of Liu Juan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu's Empress Xuanmu, née Liu, was Liu Juan's daughter.

sentences.zh: 登國初，納為夫人，生華陰公主，後生太宗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dengguo she was taken as Lady and bore the Princess of Huayin, later Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Dengguo she became a lady and bore the Princess of Huayin, later Taizong.

sentences.zh: 后專理內事，寵待有加，以鑄金人不成，故不得登后位。

translations.literal: The empress managed inner affairs exclusively and received added favor; because the golden figure did not succeed she could not ascend to empress.
translations.idiomatic: She ran inner affairs alone and was deeply favored, but the gold figure failed and she never became empress.

sentences.zh: 魏故事，後宮產子將為儲貳，其母皆賜死。

translations.literal: By Wei precedent, when the rear palace bore a son who would be heir apparent, the mother was ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: Wei custom required the mother of an heir apparent to die.

sentences.zh: 太祖末年，后以舊法薨。

translations.literal: In Taizu's last years the empress died by the old law.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizu's last years she died under that old law.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，追尊諡號，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne he raised her posthumous title and paired her in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne he gave her a posthumous title and paired her in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 自此後宮人為帝母，皆正位配饗焉。

translations.literal: From then on every rear-palace woman who was the emperor's mother took the principal place in paired sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: After that every emperor's mother from the rear palace took the principal place in paired sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 明元昭哀皇后姚氏，姚興女也，興封西平長公主。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaogong of Emperor Mingyuan, Lady Yao, was daughter of Yao Xing; Xing enfeoffed her Princess of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan's Empress Zhaogong, née Yao, was Yao Xing's daughter; Xing made her Princess of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 太宗以后禮納之，後為夫人。

translations.literal: Taizong received her with empress rites; later she was Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong received her with empress ceremony; later she held the rank of lady.

sentences.zh: 后以鑄金人不成，未昇尊位，然帝寵幸之，出入居處，禮秩如后焉。

translations.literal: Because the golden figure did not succeed she did not rise to supreme rank, yet the emperor favored her; coming and going, dwelling and rank were as for an empress.
translations.idiomatic: The gold figure failed and she never took supreme rank, yet the emperor favored her as if she were empress in residence and ceremony.

sentences.zh: 是後猶欲正位，而后謙讓不當。

translations.literal: Afterward he still wished to establish her, but the empress declined as unfitting.
translations.idiomatic: He still wished to make her empress, but she declined as unfitting.

sentences.zh: 泰常五年薨，帝追恨之，贈皇后璽綬，而後加諡焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taichang she died; the emperor mourned with regret, bestowed empress seal and sash, and added a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the fifth year of Taichang; the emperor mourned, gave her empress seal and sash, and added a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 葬雲中金陵。

translations.literal: She was buried at Jinling in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried at Jinling in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 明元密皇后杜氏，魏郡鄴人，陽平王超之妹也。

translations.literal: Secret Empress of Emperor Mingyuan, Lady Du, was a native of Ye in Wei commandery, sister to Prince Chao of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan's Secret Empress, née Du, came from Ye in Wei commandery; she was sister to Prince Chao of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 初以良家子選入太子宮，有寵，生世祖。

translations.literal: At first, as a woman of good family, she was chosen into the crown prince's palace, won favor, and bore Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen as a woman of good family into the crown prince's palace, she won favor and bore Shizu.

sentences.zh: 及太宗即位，拜貴嬪。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne she was made Honored Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne she became honored consort.

sentences.zh: 泰常五年薨，諡曰密貴嬪，葬雲中金陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taichang she died; posthumous title Secret Honored Consort; burial at Jinling in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the fifth year of Taichang with the posthumous title Secret Honored Consort and was buried at Jinling in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，追尊號諡，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne he raised her posthumous title and paired her in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizu's accession he raised her posthumous title and gave her paired sacrifice in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 又立后廟于鄴，刺史四時薦祀。

translations.literal: He also built an empress temple at Ye; the provincial governor offered seasonal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He also built an empress temple at Ye, where the provincial governor offered seasonal sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 以魏郡太后所生之邑，復其調役。

translations.literal: Because it was the home commandery of the Great Empress Dowager's birth, corvée and levies there were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Because it was the empress dowager's native commandery, corvée and levies there were remitted.

sentences.zh: 後甘露降于廟庭。

translations.literal: Later sweet dew fell in the temple courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Later sweet dew fell in the temple courtyard.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，[7]相州刺史高閭表修后廟，詔曰：「婦人外成，理無獨祀，陰必配陽以成天地，未聞有莘之國，立太姒之饗。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's time, [7] the provincial governor of Xiangzhou, Gao Lü, memorialized to repair the empress temple; an edict said: "Women achieve completion outward; in principle they are not sacrificed alone; yin must be paired with yang to complete Heaven and Earth; one has not heard of a temple to Tai Si in the state of Youxin.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozu's time, [7] Gao Lü, governor of Xiangzhou, asked to repair the empress temple. The edict said: "Women find completion outside the family; they are not sacrificed alone; yin must pair with yang to make Heaven and Earth whole. No one has heard of a separate feast for Tai Si in the state of Youxin.

sentences.zh: 此乃先皇所立，一時之至感，非經世之遠制，便可罷祀。」

translations.literal: This was what the late emperor established—a moment's utmost feeling, not a far-reaching institutional rule; the sacrifices may cease."
translations.idiomatic: This was the late emperor's moment of feeling, not eternal law; let the separate sacrifices cease."

sentences.zh: 太武皇后赫連氏，赫連屈丐女也。

translations.literal: Empress of Emperor Taiwu, Lady Helian, was daughter of Helian Qubuq.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu's empress, née Helian, was Helian Qubuq's daughter.

sentences.zh: 世祖平統萬，納后及二妹俱為貴人，後立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Shizu pacified Tongwan he took the empress and two younger sisters as honored persons; later she was made empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu took Tongwan he made the empress and her two younger sisters honored persons; later she became empress.

sentences.zh: 高宗初崩，祔葬金陵。

translations.literal: When Gaozong first died she was associated in burial at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong first died she was associated in burial at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 太武敬哀皇后賀氏，代人也。

translations.literal: Empress Jing'ai of Emperor Taiwu, Lady He, was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu's Empress Jing'ai, née He, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 初為夫人，生恭宗。

translations.literal: At first she was Lady and bore Gongzong.
translations.idiomatic: At first she was a lady and bore Gongzong.

sentences.zh: 神䴥元年薨，追贈貴嬪，葬雲中金陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenju she died; posthumously made Honored Consort; burial at Jinling in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the first year of Shenju, was posthumously made honored consort, and was buried at Jinling in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 後追加號諡，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: Later her title and posthumous name were added and she was paired in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Later her title was raised and she was paired in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 景穆恭皇后郁久閭氏，河東王毗妹也。

translations.literal: Empress Gong of Jingmu, Lady Yujiulü, was sister to Prince Pi of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmu's Empress Gong, née Yujiulü, was sister to Prince Pi of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 少以選入東宮，有寵。

translations.literal: In youth she was chosen into the Eastern Palace and won favor.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen young into the eastern palace, she won favor.

sentences.zh: 真君元年，生高宗。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenjun she bore Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenjun she bore Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 世祖末年薨。

translations.literal: In Shizu's last years she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Shizu's last years.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，追尊號諡。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne he raised her posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne he raised her posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 葬雲中金陵，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: Burial at Jinling in Yunzhong; paired sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried at Jinling in Yunzhong and paired in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 高宗乳母常氏，本遼西人。

translations.literal: Gaozong's wet-nurse Lady Chang was originally from Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong's wet-nurse, Lady Chang, came from Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 太延中，以事入宮，世祖選乳高宗。

translations.literal: In Taiyan she entered the palace on business; Shizu chose her to nurse Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyan she entered the palace; Shizu chose her to nurse Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 慈和履順，有劬勞保護之功。

translations.literal: Kind and compliant in conduct, she had merit in toilsome care and protection.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and dutiful, she earned merit through exhausting care.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，尊為保太后，尋為皇太后，謁於郊廟。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne she was honored as Foster Empress Dowager, soon Empress Dowager, with rites at the suburban altars.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne she was honored foster empress dowager, then empress dowager, with rites at the suburban altars.

sentences.zh: 和平元年崩，詔天下大臨三日，諡曰昭，葬於廣寧磨笄山，俗謂之鳴雞山，太后遺志也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Heping she died; an edict ordered three days of great mourning throughout the realm; posthumous title Zhao; burial at Mojie Mountain in Guangning—popularly called Cock-crow Mountain—by the empress dowager's own wish.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the first year of Heping; the realm mourned three days; posthumous title Zhao; she was buried at Mojie Mountain in Guangning, popularly Cock-crow Mountain, as she had wished.

sentences.zh: 依惠太后故事，別立寢廟，置守陵二百家，樹碑頌德。

translations.literal: Following Foster Empress Dowager Hui's precedent, a separate sleeping temple was built; two hundred households were set to guard the tomb; a stele praised her virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Following Foster Empress Dowager Hui's precedent, a separate temple was built, two hundred households guarded the tomb, and a stele praised her virtue.

sentences.zh: 文成文明皇后馮氏，長樂信都人也。

translations.literal: Empress Wenhua of Emperor Wencheng, Lady Feng, was a native of Xindu in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng's Empress Wenhua, née Feng, came from Xindu in Changle.

sentences.zh: 父朗，秦、雍二州刺史、西城郡公，[8]母樂浪王氏。

translations.literal: Her father Lang was governor of Qin and Yong provinces and Duke of Xicheng; [8] her mother was Lady Wang of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Lang was governor of Qin and Yong and duke of Xicheng; [8] her mother was Lady Wang of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 后生於長安，有神光之異。

translations.literal: The empress was born at Chang'an; there was a wonder of divine light.
translations.idiomatic: She was born at Chang'an amid a wonder of divine light.

sentences.zh: 朗坐事誅，后遂入宮。

translations.literal: Lang was executed for an offense; the empress then entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Lang was executed for a crime she entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 世祖左昭儀，后之姑也，雅有母德，撫養教訓。

translations.literal: Shizu's Left Worthy Lady was the empress's aunt; she had true motherly virtue in rearing and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu's left worthy lady was her aunt and raised her with motherly care.

sentences.zh: 年十四，高宗踐極，以選為貴人，後立為皇后。

translations.literal: At fourteen, when Gaozong took the throne, she was chosen Honored Person; later she was made empress.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen, when Gaozong took the throne, she became honored person; later empress.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，故事：國有大喪，三日之後，御服器物一以燒焚，百官及中宮皆號泣而臨之。

translations.literal: When Gaozong died, by precedent: on great mourning, after three days all imperial garments and vessels were burned; officials and the inner palace all wailed and attended.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong died, precedent held that after three days all imperial garments and vessels were burned while officials and the inner palace wailed over them.

sentences.zh: 后悲叫自投火中，左右救之，良久乃蘇。

translations.literal: The empress in grief threw herself into the fire; attendants saved her; long before she revived.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving, she threw herself into the fire; attendants pulled her out; long passed before she revived.

sentences.zh: 顯祖即位，尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Xianzu took the throne she was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzu took the throne she was honored empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 丞相乙渾謀逆，顯祖年十二，[9]居于諒闇，太后密定大策，誅渾，遂臨朝聽政。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Yi Hun plotted rebellion; Xianzu was twelve, [9] in the mourning hut; the empress dowager secretly settled the great plan, executed Hun, and then held court and heard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Yi Hun plotted treason; Xianzu was twelve, [9] in mourning seclusion; the empress dowager secretly settled the plot, killed Hun, and took the regency.

sentences.zh: 及高祖生，太后躬親撫養。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was born the empress dowager personally reared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was born she reared him herself.

sentences.zh: 是後罷令，不聽政事。

translations.literal: Afterward she ceased edicts and did not hear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward she stopped issuing edicts and withdrew from government.

sentences.zh: 太后行不正，內寵李弈，顯祖因事誅之，太后不得意。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's conduct was improper; she favored Li Yi within; Xianzu executed him on a pretext; the empress dowager was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: She kept an improper favorite, Li Yi; Xianzu killed him on a pretext; she was displeased.

sentences.zh: 顯祖暴崩，時言太后為之也。

translations.literal: Xianzu died suddenly; at the time people said the empress dowager had done it.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu died suddenly; rumor said the empress dowager was responsible.

sentences.zh: 承明元年，尊曰太皇太后，復臨朝聽政。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chengming she was honored Grand Empress Dowager and again held court and heard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chengming she became grand empress dowager and ruled again.

sentences.zh: 太后性聰達，自入宮掖，粗學書計。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was intelligent and penetrating; from entering the rear palace she had roughly learned writing and reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and penetrating, she had learned basic writing and reckoning in the palace.

sentences.zh: 及登尊極，省決萬機。

translations.literal: When she reached supreme rank she decided the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At supreme rank she decided every affair of state.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔曰：「朕以虛寡，幼纂寶歷，仰恃慈明，緝寧四海，欲報之德，正覺是憑，諸鷙鳥傷生之類，宜放之山林。

translations.literal: Gaozu's edict said: "We, empty and few, in youth inherited the precious succession, relying on motherly clarity to settle the four seas; to repay such virtue only the true awakening suffices; all birds of prey and creatures that harm life should be released to mountains and forests.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu decreed: "We inherited the throne young, relying on her clarity to settle the realm; to repay her virtue we release birds of prey and all creatures that harm life to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 其以此地為太皇太后經始靈塔。

translations.literal: Let this place be the site where the Grand Empress Dowager first raised her spirit pagoda.
translations.idiomatic: Let this ground be where the grand empress dowager first raised her spirit pagoda."

sentences.zh: 」於是罷鷹師曹，以其地為報德佛寺。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Hawk Office was abolished and the land became Repaying Virtue Buddhist Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The hawk office was abolished and the land became Repaying Virtue Buddhist Temple.

sentences.zh: 太后與高祖遊于方山，顧瞻川阜，有終焉之志，因謂羣臣曰：「舜葬蒼梧，二妃不從。

translations.literal: The empress dowager toured Mount Fang with Gaozu; gazing at rivers and hills she had the will to end her days there, and said to the ministers: "When Shun was buried at Cangwu, the two consorts did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Mount Fang with Gaozu she looked on river and hill and chose it for her rest, telling the ministers: "When Shun was buried at Cangwu his two consorts did not follow.

sentences.zh: 豈必遠祔山陵，然後為貴哉！

translations.literal: Must one be buried far at the imperial tombs to be honored?
translations.idiomatic: Must one lie far at the imperial tombs to be honored?"

sentences.zh: 吾百年之後，神其安此。

translations.literal: After my hundred years let my spirit rest here.
translations.idiomatic: When my hundred years are done let my spirit rest here."

sentences.zh: 」高祖乃詔有司營建壽陵於方山，又起永固石室，將終為清廟焉。

translations.literal: Gaozu then ordered the offices to build her longevity tomb at Mount Fang and raise the Eternal Firm stone hall, intending it ultimately as a pure temple.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered her longevity tomb built at Mount Fang and the Eternal Firm stone hall raised, meant in the end as a pure temple.

sentences.zh: 太和五年起作，八年而成，刊石立碑，頌太后功德。

translations.literal: Construction began in the fifth year of Taihe and was finished in the eighth; stone was carved and a stele set up praising the empress dowager's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Work began in the fifth year of Taihe and finished in the eighth; stone was carved and a stele praised her merit.

sentences.zh: 太后以高祖富於春秋，乃作勸戒歌三百餘章，又作皇誥十八篇，文多不載。

translations.literal: Because Gaozu was in the prime of youth the empress dowager composed more than three hundred chapters of admonitory songs and eighteen chapters of imperial instructions; most of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was young she wrote more than three hundred admonitory songs and eighteen imperial instructions; most are not preserved.

sentences.zh: 太后立文宣王廟於長安，[10]又立思燕佛圖於龍城，皆刊石立碑。

translations.literal: The empress dowager built the temple of Prince Wenhua at Chang'an, [10] and also the Siyan Buddha hall at Longcheng; both had stone carved and steles set up.
translations.idiomatic: She built Prince Wenhua's temple at Chang'an [10] and the Siyan Buddha hall at Longcheng, each with carved stone and stele.

sentences.zh: 太后又制，內屬五廟之孫，外戚六親緦麻，皆受復除。

translations.literal: The empress dowager also decreed: inner five-temple grandsons and outer kin within six degrees of mourning all received mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: She also decreed mourning leave for inner five-temple grandsons and outer kin within six degrees.

sentences.zh: 性儉素，不好華飾，躬御縵繒而已。

translations.literal: By nature frugal and plain, she disliked ornament and wore only plain silk herself.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal by nature, she disliked ornament and wore only plain silk.

sentences.zh: 宰人上膳，案裁徑尺，羞膳滋味減於故事十分之八。

translations.literal: When stewards served food the tray was barely a foot across; delicacies were reduced to eight-tenths of precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Trays for her meals were barely a foot wide; delicacies were cut to eight-tenths of precedent.

sentences.zh: 太后嘗以體不安，服菴䕡子。

translations.literal: The empress dowager once, feeling unwell, took crow-dipper seeds.
translations.idiomatic: Once, feeling unwell, she took crow-dipper seeds.

sentences.zh: 宰人昏而進粥，有蝘蜓在焉，后舉匕得之。

translations.literal: A steward at dusk brought porridge; a gecko was in it; the empress raised her spoon and found it.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk a steward brought porridge with a gecko in it; she found it with her spoon.

sentences.zh: 高祖侍側，大怒，將加極罰，太后笑而釋之。

translations.literal: Gaozu attended at her side, greatly angered, and meant extreme punishment; the empress dowager smiled and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu beside her was furious and meant extreme punishment; she smiled and let the man go.

sentences.zh: 自太后臨朝專政，高祖雅性孝謹，不欲參決，事無巨細，一禀於太后。

translations.literal: From the empress dowager's sole regency Gaozu by nature was filial and cautious and did not wish to decide; whether great or small, all followed the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Under her sole rule Gaozu was filial and cautious and would not decide; great and small, all went to her.

sentences.zh: 太后多智略，猜忍，能行大事，生殺賞罰，決之俄頃，多有不關高祖者。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was resourceful, suspicious, and cruel, able to act on great matters; life, death, reward, and punishment were decided in a moment, often without Gaozu's knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: She was resourceful, suspicious, and cruel, deciding life, death, reward, and punishment in a moment, often without telling Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 是以威福兼作，震動內外。

translations.literal: Thus authority and favor together shook inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: Authority and favor together shook court and realm.

sentences.zh: 故𣏌道德、王遇、張祐、苻承祖等拔自微閹，歲中而至王公；

translations.literal: Thus Wang Yu, Zhang You, Fu Chengzu, and others were raised from humble eunuchs to princes and dukes within the year;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, Zhang You, Fu Chengzu, and others rose from humble eunuchs to princes and dukes within a year;

sentences.zh: 王叡出入臥內，數年便為宰輔，賞賚財帛以千萬億計，金書鐵券，許以不死之詔。

translations.literal: Wang Rui went in and out of the sleeping quarters; within years he was chief minister; rewards of wealth in the hundreds of millions; golden writ on iron covenant promising an edict of deathlessness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rui entered the sleeping quarters and within years became chief minister, rewarded with wealth in the hundreds of millions and a golden writ on iron promising he could not be executed.

sentences.zh: 李沖雖以器能受任，亦由見寵帷幄，密加錫賚，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Though Li Chong was employed for ability, it was also through favor within the curtains and secret bestowals beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong won office for talent, but also through secret favor and gifts beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 后性嚴明，假有寵待，亦無所縱。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's nature was strict and clear; even when she showed favor she did not indulge.
translations.idiomatic: She was strict and clear; even favorites were not indulged.

sentences.zh: 左右纖介之愆，動加捶楚，多至百餘，少亦數十。

translations.literal: For the slightest fault of attendants she often added beating—more than a hundred strokes, fewer several tens.
translations.idiomatic: The slightest fault in attendants could bring a hundred strokes or several tens.

sentences.zh: 然性不宿憾，尋亦待之如初，或因此更加富貴。

translations.literal: Yet she did not harbor old resentment; soon she treated them as before, or they grew richer for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet she did not hold grudges; soon she treated them as before, or they grew richer.

sentences.zh: 是以人人懷於利欲，至死而不思退。

translations.literal: Thus everyone clung to profit and desire and to the end did not think of withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone clung to profit and never thought of leaving.

sentences.zh: 太后曾與高祖幸靈泉池，燕羣臣及藩國使人、諸方渠帥，各令為其方舞。

translations.literal: The empress dowager once with Gaozu visited Spirit Spring Pool, feasted ministers and envoys of border states and chieftains of all regions, each ordered to perform his region's dance.
translations.idiomatic: She once feasted ministers and foreign envoys at Spirit Spring Pool and had each perform his region's dance.

sentences.zh: 高祖帥羣臣上壽，太后忻然作歌，帝亦和歌，遂命羣臣各言其志，於是和歌者九十人。

translations.literal: Gaozu led the ministers in offering longevity; the empress dowager gladly made a song; the emperor harmonized; then she ordered each to state his aim—and ninety harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu led longevity toasts; she sang gladly; he harmonized; then each stated his aim—and ninety sang in reply.

sentences.zh: 太后外禮民望元丕、游明根等，頒賜金帛輿馬，每至褒美叡等，皆引丕等參之，以示無私。

translations.literal: The empress dowager outwardly honored men the people looked to—Yuan Pi, You Minggen, and others—and bestowed gold, silk, carriages, and horses; whenever she praised Rui and the like she had Pi and others present to show lack of partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly she honored Yuan Pi, You Minggen, and others the people respected, bestowing gold and horses; when she praised Rui she had Pi present to show impartiality.

sentences.zh: 又自以過失，懼人議己，小有疑忌，便見誅戮。

translations.literal: Again, fearing criticism of her faults, at the slightest suspicion she saw execution.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing criticism, she killed at the slightest suspicion.

sentences.zh: 迄后之崩，高祖不知所生。

translations.literal: Until the empress dowager's death Gaozu did not know how he was born.
translations.idiomatic: Until her death Gaozu did not know the truth of his birth.

sentences.zh: 至如李訢、李惠之徒，猜嫌覆滅者十餘家，死者數百人，率多枉濫，天下冤之。

translations.literal: As for Li Xin, Li Hui, and the like—more than ten houses destroyed through suspicion—several hundred dead, mostly wrongful; the realm mourned them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin, Li Hui, and more than ten houses fell to suspicion; hundreds died, mostly innocent; the realm mourned them.

sentences.zh: 十四年，崩於太和殿，時年四十九。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year she died in the Taihe Hall at age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year she died in the Taihe Hall at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 其日，有雄雉集于太華殿。

translations.literal: That day a male pheasant alighted on the Taihua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That day a male pheasant alighted on the Taihua Hall.

sentences.zh: 高祖酌飲不入口五日，毀慕過禮。

translations.literal: Gaozu drank but did not eat for five days; mourning exceeded ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu drank but did not eat for five days; his mourning exceeded ritual.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文明太皇太后。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Grand Empress Dowager Wenhua.
translations.idiomatic: Her posthumous title was Grand Empress Dowager Wenhua.

sentences.zh: 葬于永固陵，日中而反，虞於鑒玄殿。

translations.literal: Burial at the Eternal Firm tomb; at midday the procession returned; offering at the Jianxuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried at the Eternal Firm tomb; at noon the procession returned; rites were at the Jianxuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「尊旨從儉，不申罔極之痛；

translations.literal: An edict said: "The honored will followed frugality; boundless grief was not expressed;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Her honored will was frugal; boundless grief could not be fully shown;

sentences.zh: 稱情允禮，仰損儉訓之德。

translations.literal: fitting feeling and allowable ritual upward diminish the teaching of frugality.
translations.idiomatic: yet fitting feeling and allowable ritual still tempered frugal teaching."

sentences.zh: 進退思惟，倍用崩感。

translations.literal: Advancing and retreating in thought, grief redoubled at the collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking it through, grief redoubled at her death.

sentences.zh: 又山陵之節，亦有成命，內則方丈，外裁揜坎，脫於孝子之心有所不盡者，室中可二丈，墳不得過三十餘步。

translations.literal: Again, for mountain-tomb rites there were settled orders: within a square zhang, without only covering the pit—yet where the filial son's heart could not be fully satisfied, the inner chamber might be two zhang and the mound not more than thirty-odd paces.
translations.idiomatic: For the tomb she had ordered a square zhang within and only a covering mound without—yet where a son's heart fell short the inner chamber might be two zhang and the mound thirty-odd paces.

sentences.zh: 今以山陵萬世所仰，復廣為六十步。

translations.literal: Now the mountain tomb is looked to for ten thousand generations and is again broadened to sixty paces.
translations.idiomatic: Now the tomb is looked to for ten thousand generations and is broadened to sixty paces.

sentences.zh: 辜負遺旨，益以痛絕。

translations.literal: Failing the last will, grief is all the more cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Failing her last will, grief cuts deeper.

sentences.zh: 其幽房大小，棺槨質約，不設明器。

translations.literal: The inner chamber's size, coffin quality plain and simple, no bright vessels set out.
translations.idiomatic: The inner chamber, coffin, and goods stay plain; no bright grave goods.

sentences.zh: 至於素帳、縵茵、瓷瓦之物，亦皆不置。

translations.literal: Even plain curtains, plain mats, porcelain tiles—none are placed.
translations.idiomatic: Even plain curtains, mats, and porcelain—none are placed.

sentences.zh: 此則遵先志，從冊令，俱奉遺事。

translations.literal: This follows the former will and the written order; both honor the legacy.
translations.idiomatic: This follows her will and the written order; both honor her legacy.

sentences.zh: 而有從有違，未達者或以致怪。

translations.literal: Yet where there is compliance and where departure, those who do not understand may find it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Where we comply and where we depart, some may find it strange.

sentences.zh: 梓宮之裏，玄堂之內，聖靈所憑，是以一一奉遵，仰昭儉德。

translations.literal: Within the imperial coffin, in the dark hall, the sage spirit relies—therefore each point is followed to display frugal virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Within the coffin and dark hall her spirit rests—there we follow each point to show frugal virtue.

sentences.zh: 其餘外事，有所不從，以盡痛慕之情。

translations.literal: For other outer matters where there is non-compliance, it is to exhaust the feeling of painful longing.
translations.idiomatic: Outer matters we bend to exhaust painful longing.

sentences.zh: 其宣示遠近，著告羣司，上明儉誨之善，下彰違命之失。

translations.literal: Let this be proclaimed far and near and set forth to all offices: above to clarify the good of frugal teaching, below to show the fault of disobeying the command."
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed far and near: above to clarify frugal teaching, below to show where we disobeyed."

sentences.zh: 」及卒哭，孝文服衰，近臣從服，三司已下外臣衰服者，變服就練，七品已下盡除即吉。

translations.literal: At the end of wailing Gaozu wore mourning; close attendants followed; third-rank ministers and below in outer mourning changed to finer hemp; seventh-rank and below removed mourning and returned to normal dress.
translations.idiomatic: After wailing Gaozu wore mourning; close attendants followed; outer officials third rank and below changed to finer hemp; seventh rank and below returned to normal dress.

sentences.zh: 設祔祭於太和殿，公卿已下始親公事。

translations.literal: Associated sacrifice was set in the Taihe Hall; from dukes and ministers down they first attended to public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Associated sacrifice was set in the Taihe Hall; from dukes down they resumed public business.

sentences.zh: 高祖毀瘠，絕酒肉，不內御者三年。

translations.literal: Gaozu wasted away, abstained from wine and meat, and did not take inner attendants for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wasted away, took no wine or meat, and kept no inner attendants for three years.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖孝於太后，乃於永固陵東北里餘，豫營壽宮，有終焉瞻望之志。

translations.literal: At first Gaozu was filial toward the empress dowager; therefore a little more than a li northeast of the Eternal Firm tomb he beforehand built a longevity palace, with the will to gaze there at the end.
translations.idiomatic: Filial toward her, he had built a longevity palace a little over a li northeast of her tomb, intending to rest his gaze there at the end.

sentences.zh: 及遷洛陽，乃自表瀍西以為山園之所，而方山虛宮至今猶存，號曰「萬年堂」云。

translations.literal: When he moved the capital to Luoyang he himself memorialized the west bank of the Chan as the mountain garden site; the empty hall at Mount Fang remains to this day, called the Hall of Ten Thousand Years.
translations.idiomatic: When he moved to Luoyang he chose the west bank of the Chan for his own mountain garden; the empty hall at Mount Fang remains, called the Hall of Ten Thousand Years.

sentences.zh: 文成元皇后李氏，梁國蒙縣人，頓丘王峻之妹也。

translations.literal: Primary Empress of Emperor Wencheng, Lady Li, was a native of Meng in Liang; sister to Prince Jun of Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng's primary empress, née Li, came from Meng in Liang; she was sister to Prince Jun of Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: [11]后之生也，有異於常，父方叔恒言此女當大貴。

translations.literal: [11] At her birth there was wonder beyond the usual; her father Fangshu always said this girl would be greatly honored.
translations.idiomatic: [11] Her birth was wondrous; her father Fangshu always said she would rise to great honor.

sentences.zh: 及長，姿質美麗。

translations.literal: When grown, her bearing and beauty were fine.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, she was beautiful in bearing.

sentences.zh: 世祖南征，永昌王仁出壽春，軍至后宅，因得后。

translations.literal: When Shizu campaigned south, Prince Yongchang Ren marched from Shouchun; the army reached her home and took her.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu marched south, Prince Yongchang Ren left Shouchun; his army reached her home and took her.

sentences.zh: 及仁鎮長安，遇事誅，后與其家人送平城宮。

translations.literal: When Ren was stationed at Chang'an he was executed for an affair; she and her family were sent to the palace at Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren was stationed at Chang'an he was executed; she and her family were sent to the Pingcheng palace.

sentences.zh: 高宗登白樓望見，美之，謂左右曰：「此婦人佳乎？

translations.literal: Gaozong ascended the White Tower, saw her, admired her, and said to attendants: "Is this woman not fine?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong on the White Tower saw her, admired her, and asked attendants: "Is she not fine?"

sentences.zh: 」左右咸曰「然」。

translations.literal: All said "Indeed."
translations.idiomatic: All said, "Indeed."

sentences.zh: 乃下臺，后得幸於齋庫中，遂有娠。

translations.literal: He descended; she won favor in the fasting storehouse and became pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: He descended; she won favor in the fasting storehouse and became pregnant.

sentences.zh: 常太后後問后，后云：「為帝所幸，仍有娠。

translations.literal: Foster Empress Dowager Chang later questioned her; she said: "The emperor favored me and I am still pregnant."
translations.idiomatic: Foster Empress Dowager Chang later questioned her; she said the emperor had favored her and she was pregnant.

sentences.zh: 」時守庫者亦私書壁記之，別加驗問，皆相符同。

translations.literal: The storekeeper had also privately written on the wall; separate questioning matched in every point.
translations.idiomatic: The storekeeper had privately written on the wall; separate questioning matched.

sentences.zh: 及生顯祖，拜貴人。

translations.literal: When she bore Xianzu she was made Honored Person.
translations.idiomatic: When she bore Xianzu she was made honored person.

sentences.zh: 太安二年，太后令依故事，令后具條記在南兄弟及引所結宗兄洪之，悉以付託。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tai'an the empress dowager ordered by precedent that the empress fully record her brothers in the south and sworn clan brother Hongzhi, all to be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tai'an the empress dowager ordered her, by precedent, to record her southern brothers and sworn clan brother Hongzhi for entrustment.

sentences.zh: 臨訣，每一稱兄弟，輒拊胸慟泣，遂薨。

translations.literal: At the farewell, each time she named a brother she beat her breast and wept bitterly; then she died.
translations.idiomatic: At the farewell each brother's name brought breast-beating tears; then she died.

sentences.zh: 後諡曰元皇后，葬金陵，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: Later posthumous title Primary Empress; burial at Jinling; paired sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Later she received the posthumous title Primary Empress, burial at Jinling, and pairing in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 獻文思皇后李氏，中山安喜人，南郡王惠之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Si of Emperor Xianwen, Lady Li, was a native of Anxi in Zhongshan; daughter of Prince Hui of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen's Empress Si, née Li, came from Anxi in Zhongshan; daughter of Prince Hui of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 姿德婉淑，年十八，以選入東宮。

translations.literal: Graceful in bearing and virtue, at eighteen she was chosen into the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful in bearing and virtue, at eighteen she entered the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 顯祖即位，為夫人，生高祖。

translations.literal: When Xianzu took the throne she was Lady and bore Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzu took the throne she was a lady and bore Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 皇興三年薨，上下莫不悼惜。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangxing she died; above and below none did not mourn.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huangxing she died; court and realm mourned.

sentences.zh: 葬金陵。

translations.literal: Burial was at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 承明元年追崇號諡，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenming her title and posthumous name were elevated, and she received joint offerings in the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenming year 1 her honors and posthumous title were raised, and she was given joint sacrifice in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 孝文貞皇后林氏，平原人也。

translations.literal: Empress Zhen of Emperor Wen, the Lin clan, was a native of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhen of Emperor Wen, née Lin, came from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: [12]叔父金閭，起自閹官，有寵於常太后，官至尚書、平涼公。

translations.literal: [12] Her uncle Jinlu rose from the eunuch ranks, won favor with Empress Dowager Chang, and reached the posts of Master of Writing and Duke of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: [12] Her uncle Jinlu had risen from the eunuch service, won favor with Empress Dowager Chang, and rose to Master of Writing and Duke of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 金閭兄勝為平涼太守。

translations.literal: Jinlu's elder brother Sheng was administrator of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Jinlu's elder brother Sheng served as administrator of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 金閭，顯祖初為定州刺史。

translations.literal: Jinlu, at the beginning of Emperor Xianzu's reign, was regional inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xianzu's reign Jinlu was made regional inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾為乙渾所誅，兄弟皆死。

translations.literal: Before long he was executed by Yi Hun, and the brothers all died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was killed by Yi Hun, and the brothers all perished.

sentences.zh: 勝無子，有二女，入掖庭。

translations.literal: Sheng had no sons but two daughters, who entered the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had no sons; his two daughters were sent into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 后容色美麗，得幸於高祖，生皇子恂。

translations.literal: The empress was beautiful in face and form, won Gaozu's favor, and bore the prince Xun.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was strikingly beautiful, found favor with Emperor Gaozu, and bore Prince Xun.

sentences.zh: 以恂將為儲貳，太和七年后依舊制薨。

translations.literal: Because Xun was to be heir apparent, in the seventh year of Taihe the empress died according to the old custom.
translations.idiomatic: As Xun was to be crown prince, in Taihe year 7 the empress died under the old custom.

sentences.zh: 高祖仁恕，不欲襲前事，而禀文明太后意，故不果行。

translations.literal: Gaozu was humane and forbearing and did not wish to repeat former deeds, yet he followed Empress Dowager Wenming's intent, so it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was merciful and unwilling to repeat the old practice, but he deferred to Empress Dowager Wenming, and the custom was not enforced.

sentences.zh: 諡曰貞皇后，葬金陵。

translations.literal: Her posthumous title was Empress Zhen, and she was buried at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: She was given the posthumous name Empress Zhen and buried at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 及恂以罪賜死，有司奏追廢后為庶人。

translations.literal: When Xun was ordered to die for his crimes, the authorities memorialized to strip the empress posthumously and reduce her to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun was condemned and ordered to die, the authorities petitioned to posthumously depose the empress as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 孝文廢皇后馮氏，太師熙之女也。

translations.literal: The deposed empress of Emperor Wen, the Feng clan, was a daughter of Grand Preceptor Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's deposed empress, née Feng, was a daughter of Grand Preceptor Xi.

sentences.zh: 太和十七年，高祖既終喪，太尉元丕等表以長秋未建，六宮無主，請正內位。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Taihe, after Gaozu had completed mourning, Grand Commandant Yuan Pi and others memorialized that the office of the empress had not been established and the six palaces had no mistress, asking that the inner rank be settled.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 17, once Gaozu had finished mourning, Grand Commandant Yuan Pi and others submitted that with no empress installed and the six palaces without a head, the inner court should be regularized.

sentences.zh: 高祖從之，立后為皇后。

translations.literal: Gaozu assented and installed her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu agreed and made her empress.

sentences.zh: 高祖每遵典禮，后及夫、嬪以下接御皆以次進。

translations.literal: Whenever Gaozu observed ritual, the empress and consorts and concubines below all attended him in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu always kept to ritual: the empress, consorts, and lower concubines all came to him in proper order.

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，后留京師。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, the empress remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaigns the empress stayed behind in the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖又南征，后率六宮遷洛陽。

translations.literal: When Gaozu campaigned south again, the empress led the six palaces in moving to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On another southern expedition the empress led the six palaces in relocating to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及后父熙、兄誕薨，高祖為書慰以敍哀情。

translations.literal: When the empress's father Xi and elder brother Dan died, Gaozu wrote letters of consolation expressing his grief.
translations.idiomatic: When her father Xi and elder brother Dan died, Gaozu wrote to console her and voice his sorrow.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還洛，恩遇甚厚。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang, her favor was very great.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Luoyang, she enjoyed exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 高祖後重引后姊昭儀至洛，稍有寵，后禮愛漸衰。

translations.literal: Later Gaozu again summoned the empress's elder sister, a lady of bright demeanor, to Luoyang; she gradually won favor, and the empress's courtesy and affection waned.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gaozu brought the empress's elder sister, already a zhaoyi, back to Luoyang; as the sister gained favor, the empress's standing slowly faded.

sentences.zh: 昭儀自以年長，且前入宮掖，素見待念，輕后而不率妾禮。

translations.literal: The zhaoyi considered herself older and having entered the palace earlier, was long treated with regard, looked down on the empress, and would not observe a concubine's rites.
translations.idiomatic: The zhaoyi, being older and having entered the palace earlier, had long been favored; she slighted the empress and refused the deference owed a junior wife.

sentences.zh: 后雖性不妬忌，時有愧恨之色。

translations.literal: Though the empress was not jealous by nature, at times she showed shame and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Though not jealous by nature, the empress sometimes showed shame and bitterness.

sentences.zh: 昭儀規為內主，譖構百端。

translations.literal: The zhaoyi plotted to become mistress of the inner court and slandered her in every way.
translations.idiomatic: The zhaoyi schemed to rule the inner palace and wove slander on every side.

sentences.zh: 尋廢后為庶人。

translations.literal: Before long the empress was deposed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the empress was deposed and reduced to a commoner.

sentences.zh: 后貞謹有德操，遂為練行尼。

translations.literal: The empress was chaste, careful, and possessed moral conduct; she then became a nun in plain practice.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste and principled, she took the tonsure as a nun in austere practice.

sentences.zh: 後終於瑤光佛寺。

translations.literal: Later she died at Yaoguang Buddhist Temple.
translations.idiomatic: She ended her days at Yaoguang Temple.

sentences.zh: 孝文幽皇后，亦馮熙女。

translations.literal: Empress You of Emperor Wen was also a daughter of Feng Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress You of Emperor Wen was likewise a daughter of Feng Xi.

sentences.zh: 母曰常氏，本微賤，得幸於熙，熙元妃公主薨後，遂主家事。

translations.literal: Her mother was the Chang clan, originally of low station; she won Xi's favor, and after Xi's primary consort the princess died, she took charge of the household.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother, née Chang, was of humble birth; favored by Xi, after his principal consort the princess died she managed the household.

sentences.zh: 生后與北平公夙。

translations.literal: She bore the empress and Beiping Duke Su.
translations.idiomatic: She bore the future empress and Beiping Duke Su.

sentences.zh: 文明太皇太后欲家世貴寵，乃簡熙二女俱入掖庭，時年十四。

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager Wenming wished the family honored and favored, so she selected both of Xi's daughters to enter the inner palace; they were fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Empress Dowager Wenming wanted the Feng house ennobled, so both of Xi's daughters were chosen for the inner palace at age fourteen.

sentences.zh: 其一早卒。

translations.literal: One died early.
translations.idiomatic: One of them died young.

sentences.zh: 后有姿媚，偏見愛幸。

translations.literal: The empress had charm and grace and was especially loved and favored.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was alluring and won special favor.

sentences.zh: 未幾疾病，文明太后乃遣還家為尼，高祖猶留念焉。

translations.literal: Before long she fell ill; Empress Dowager Wenming sent her home to become a nun, yet Gaozu still kept her in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she fell ill; Empress Dowager Wenming sent her home to take the veil, though Gaozu still thought of her.

sentences.zh: 歲餘而太后崩。

translations.literal: After a year and more the empress dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 高祖服終，頗存訪之，又聞后素疹痊除，遣閹官雙三念璽書勞問，遂迎赴洛陽。

translations.literal: When Gaozu finished mourning he still sought her; hearing her chronic rash had cleared, he sent the eunuch Shuang Sannian with an imperial letter of inquiry and welcomed her to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended Gaozu still sought her; learning her chronic rash had healed, he sent the eunuch Shuang Sannian with an imperial message and had her brought to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及至，寵愛過初，專寢當夕，宮人稀復進見。

translations.literal: When she arrived, favor exceeded the first time; she alone shared his bed each night, and palace women rarely saw him again.
translations.idiomatic: On her arrival favor surpassed the first reign; she alone shared his nights, and other palace women seldom gained audience.

sentences.zh: 拜為左昭儀，後立為皇后。

translations.literal: She was appointed left zhaoyi, then later installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: She was made left zhaoyi and later elevated to empress.

sentences.zh: 始以疾歸，頗有失德之聞，高祖頻歲南征，后遂與中官高菩薩私亂。

translations.literal: From the time she had returned home for illness there had been talk of misconduct; with Gaozu campaigning south year after year, the empress then had a secret affair with the palace attendant Gaopusa.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors of misconduct had followed her illness and return home; while Gaozu campaigned south year after year, she took the palace attendant Gaopusa as her lover.

sentences.zh: 及高祖在汝南不豫，后便公然醜恣，中常侍雙蒙等為其心腹。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was unwell at Runan, the empress then openly indulged in shameless license, and regular palace attendants Shuang Meng and others were her confidants.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu fell ill at Runan, the empress flaunted her debauchery, with Regular Palace Attendant Shuang Meng and others as her inner circle.

sentences.zh: 中常侍劇鵬諫而不從，憤懼致死。

translations.literal: Regular Palace Attendant Ju Peng remonstrated but she would not listen; in anger and fear he died.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Palace Attendant Ju Peng admonished her in vain and, stricken with anger and dread, died.

sentences.zh: 是時，彭城公主，宋王劉昶子婦也，年少嫠居。

translations.literal: At that time Princess Pengcheng, wife of the son of Prince of Song Liu Chang, was young and widowed.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Pengcheng, daughter-in-law of Prince of Song Liu Chang, was young and living as a widow.

sentences.zh: 北平公馮夙，后之同母弟也，后求婚於高祖，高祖許之。

translations.literal: Beiping Duke Feng Su, the empress's younger brother by the same mother, sought marriage through the empress; Gaozu consented.
translations.idiomatic: Beiping Duke Feng Su, her full brother, sought her help in marrying the princess; Gaozu agreed.

sentences.zh: 公主志不願，后欲強之。

translations.literal: The princess was unwilling in heart; the empress wished to force the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The princess refused, but the empress meant to compel her.

sentences.zh: 婚有日矣，公主密與侍婢及家僮十餘人，乘輕車，冒霖雨，赴懸瓠奉謁高祖，自陳本意，因言后與菩薩亂狀。

translations.literal: The wedding day was near when the princess secretly took a dozen or so maids and household servants in a light carriage, braved torrential rain, went to Xuanchi to audience Gaozu, stated her true intent, and reported the empress's affair with Pusa.
translations.idiomatic: With the wedding set, the princess secretly took a light carriage with a dozen maids and servants, rode through driving rain to Xuanchi to see Gaozu, declared her refusal, and revealed the empress's liaison with Pusa.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而駭愕，未之全信而祕匿之，惟彭城王侍疾左右，具知其事。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard this in shock and alarm, did not wholly believe it, and kept it secret; only Prince of Pengcheng attending his illness at his side knew the whole affair.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was stunned but did not fully believe her and kept the matter hidden; only Prince of Pengcheng, at his sickbed, knew everything.

sentences.zh: 此後，后漸憂懼，與母常氏求託女巫，禱厭無所不至，願高祖疾不起，一旦得如文明太后輔少主稱命者，賞報不貲。

translations.literal: Thereafter the empress grew anxious and fearful; with her mother the Chang clan she sought witches, performing every prayer and curse, wishing Gaozu's illness would not lift so that one day, like Empress Dowager Wenming aiding a young ruler and holding power, she might reward them beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the empress grew fearful; with her mother Lady Chang she turned to witches and every form of curse-prayer, hoping Gaozu would not recover so she could rule as regent like Empress Dowager Wenming and repay them lavishly.

sentences.zh: 又取三牲宮中妖祠，假言祈福，專為左道。

translations.literal: She also took the three sacrificial animals for illicit shrines in the palace, claiming prayers for blessing while devoted to heterodox ways.
translations.idiomatic: She set up illicit shrines in the palace with the three sacrificial beasts, pretending to pray for blessings while practicing forbidden rites.

sentences.zh: 母常或自詣宮中，或遣侍婢與相報答。

translations.literal: Mother Chang sometimes came to the palace herself, sometimes sent maids to exchange messages.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chang sometimes entered the palace herself, sometimes sent maids to carry messages back and forth.

sentences.zh: 高祖自豫州北幸鄴，后慮還見治檢，彌懷危怖，驟令閹人託參起居，皆賜之衣裳，殷勤託寄，勿使漏洩。

translations.literal: When Gaozu traveled north from Yuzhou to Ye, the empress feared returning to face investigation, grew ever more terrified, and repeatedly had eunuchs convey greetings on her behalf, all rewarded with garments and earnestly entrusted not to let anything leak.
translations.idiomatic: As Gaozu went north from Yuzhou to Ye, the empress, dreading investigation on his return, sent eunuchs again and again with greetings, lavished clothes on them, and begged them to keep silent.

sentences.zh: 亦令雙蒙充行，省其信不。

translations.literal: She also had Shuang Meng go along to see whether they were trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: She also sent Shuang Meng to go with them and test their loyalty.

sentences.zh: [13]然惟小黃門蘇興壽密陳委曲，高祖問其本末，敕以勿洩。

translations.literal: [13] Yet only junior yellow-gate attendant Su Xingshou secretly reported the details; Gaozu questioned him on the full story and ordered that it not be divulged.
translations.idiomatic: [13] Only junior yellow-gate attendant Su Xingshou secretly laid out the whole affair; Gaozu questioned him to the bottom and commanded secrecy.

sentences.zh: 至洛，執問菩薩、雙蒙等六人，迭相證舉，具得情狀。

translations.literal: At Luoyang, Pusa, Shuang Meng, and six others were seized and questioned; they testified against one another in turn, and the full circumstances were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang six men including Pusa and Shuang Meng were arrested; their mutual accusations brought the whole truth to light.

sentences.zh: 高祖以疾臥含溫室，夜引后，并列菩薩等於戶外。

translations.literal: Gaozu, ill and resting in the warming chamber, summoned the empress at night and had Pusa and the others lined up outside the door.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, ill in the warming chamber, summoned the empress by night and lined Pusa and the others outside the door.

sentences.zh: 后臨入，令閹人搜衣中，稍有寸刃便斬。

translations.literal: As the empress was about to enter, he ordered eunuchs to search her garments; the slightest blade meant execution.
translations.idiomatic: Before she entered he ordered eunuchs to search her; any blade, however small, meant death.

sentences.zh: 后頓首泣謝，乃賜坐東楹，去御筵二丈餘。

translations.literal: The empress kowtowed and wept in apology; then she was granted a seat on the eastern pillar, more than two zhang from the imperial mat.
translations.idiomatic: She kowtowed and wept; then she was given a seat by the eastern pillar, more than two zhang from his couch.

sentences.zh: 高祖令菩薩等陳狀，又讓后曰：「汝母有妖術，可具言之。

translations.literal: Gaozu had Pusa and the others state the facts, then reproached the empress: "Your mother practices sorcery—you must tell it fully.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made Pusa and the others confess, then rebuked the empress: "Your mother uses witchcraft—speak of it in full.

sentences.zh: 」后乞屏左右，有所密啟。

translations.literal: " The empress begged to dismiss those present and had something to report in secret.
translations.idiomatic: " She begged to dismiss attendants and speak privately.

sentences.zh: 高祖敕中侍悉出，唯令長秋卿白整在側，取衞直刀柱之，后猶不言。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered all central attendants out, keeping only Director of the Long Autumn Bureau Bai Zheng at his side, took a guard's straight blade and held it upright; the empress still would not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent the central attendants away, keeping only Director of the Long Autumn Bai Zheng beside him with a guard's blade held upright; still she would not speak.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃以綿堅塞整耳，自小語呼整再三，無所應，乃令后言。

translations.literal: Gaozu then stuffed Bai Zheng's ears tightly with cotton, called to Zheng softly again and again, and getting no answer, ordered the empress to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu stuffed cotton into Zheng's ears, whispered his name repeatedly without reply, and then commanded the empress to speak.

sentences.zh: 事隱，人莫知之。

translations.literal: The matter was concealed; no one knew it.
translations.idiomatic: What she said remained hidden; no one else knew.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃喚彭城、北海二王令入坐，言：「昔是汝嫂，今乃他人，但入勿避。

translations.literal: Gaozu then summoned the princes of Pengcheng and Beihai to enter and sit, saying: "Once she was your sister-in-law; now she is another's person—enter and do not shrink.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu called in the princes of Pengcheng and Beihai and said: "Once she was your sister-in-law; now she is a stranger—come in and do not hold back.

sentences.zh: 」二王固辭，不獲命。

translations.literal: " The two princes firmly declined but could not refuse the command.
translations.idiomatic: " Both princes refused but could not disobey.

sentences.zh: 及入，高祖云：「此老嫗乃欲白刃插我肋上！

translations.literal: When they entered, Gaozu said: "This old woman meant to drive a bare blade into my ribs!
translations.idiomatic: Once inside Gaozu said: "This old woman meant to put a blade in my ribs!

sentences.zh: 可窮問本末，勿有所難。

translations.literal: Question her to the end on how it began and ended; hold nothing back.
translations.idiomatic: Press her for the full story and spare nothing.

sentences.zh: 」高祖深自引過，致愧二王。

translations.literal: " Gaozu deeply blamed himself and expressed shame before the two princes.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu took the blame upon himself and apologized to the two princes.

sentences.zh: 又云：「馮家女不能復相廢逐，且使在宮中空坐，有心乃能自死，汝等勿謂吾猶有情也。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Feng girl cannot again be deposed and driven out; for now let her sit idle in the palace—if she has the heart she can die by herself. Do not think I still have affection.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "The Feng girl will not be deposed again; let her sit empty in the palace—if she has the will she can die herself. Do not imagine I still care.

sentences.zh: 」高祖素至孝，猶以文明太后故，未便行廢。

translations.literal: " Gaozu was by nature most filial; still for Empress Dowager Wenming's sake he did not yet carry out deposition.
translations.idiomatic: " Filial as he was, he still would not depose her out of regard for Empress Dowager Wenming.

sentences.zh: 良久，二王出，乃賜后辭死訣。

translations.literal: After a long while the two princes withdrew, and he then gave the empress a parting message before death.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the princes left, and he sent the empress a final farewell.

sentences.zh: [14]再拜稽首，涕泣歔欷。

translations.literal: [14] She bowed again, touched her head to the ground, and wept with sobs and sighs.
translations.idiomatic: [14] She bowed again to the ground, weeping and sighing.

sentences.zh: 令入東房。

translations.literal: He ordered her into the eastern room.
translations.idiomatic: He had her enter the eastern chamber.

sentences.zh: 及入宮後，帝命閹人有所問於后，后罵曰：「天子婦，親面對，豈令汝傳也！

translations.literal: After she entered the palace, the emperor ordered a eunuch to question the empress; the empress cursed: "I am the Son of Heaven's wife—should I face him in person, or have you relay words!
translations.idiomatic: After she was inside, the emperor sent a eunuch to question her; she raged: "I am the emperor's wife—should I not speak to him face to face rather than through you!

sentences.zh: 」高祖怒，敕后母常入，與后杖，常撻之百餘乃止。

translations.literal: " Gaozu was angry and ordered the empress's mother Chang to enter and beat her with rods; Chang flogged her more than a hundred times before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu in anger summoned her mother Lady Chang to beat her with rods; Chang lashed her more than a hundred strokes before stopping.

sentences.zh: 高祖尋南伐，后留京師，雖以罪失寵，而夫人嬪妾奉之如法，惟令世宗在東宮，無朝謁之事。

translations.literal: Gaozu soon campaigned south; the empress remained in the capital. Though she had lost favor for her crimes, ladies and concubines still served her according to ritual; only Crown Prince Xuanzong in the eastern palace was barred from court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu soon marched south again; though disgraced, she was still treated by consorts according to rite, while Crown Prince Xuanzong in the eastern palace was forbidden court audiences.

sentences.zh: 高祖疾甚，謂彭城王勰曰：「後宮久乖陰德，自絕於天。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was gravely ill he told Prince of Pengcheng Xie: "The inner palace has long violated feminine virtue and cut itself off from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Near death Gaozu told Prince of Pengcheng Xie: "The inner palace has long violated its proper virtue and turned from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 若不早為之所，恐成漢末故事。

translations.literal: If we do not deal with this early, I fear it will become the story of the late Han.
