translations.idiomatic: If we do not act soon, I fear another tale like the end of Han.

sentences.zh: 吾死之後，可賜自盡別宮，葬以后禮，庶掩馮門之大過。

translations.literal: After my death, grant her suicide in a separate palace and bury her with empress rites, that the Feng house's great fault may be covered.
translations.idiomatic: After I die, let her take poison in a separate palace and bury her with empress honors, to cover the Feng clan's shame.

sentences.zh: 」高祖崩，梓宮達魯陽，乃行遺詔。

translations.literal: " When Gaozu died and the coffin reached Luyang, the testament was then carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " When Gaozu died and the coffin reached Luyang, his final testament was executed.

sentences.zh: 北海王詳奉宣遺旨，長秋卿白整等入授后藥，后走呼不肯引決，曰：「官豈有此也，是諸王輩殺我耳！

translations.literal: Prince of Beihai Xiang, carrying out the testament, and Director of the Long Autumn Bai Zheng and others entered to give the empress poison; she ran shouting and refused to take her leave, saying: "Would the ruler truly do this? It is those princes killing me!
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Beihai Xiang proclaimed the testament; Bai Zheng and others brought poison; she fled shouting and would not die, crying: "Would the throne do this? Those princes are killing me!

sentences.zh: 」整等執持，強之，乃含椒而盡。

translations.literal: " Zheng and the others seized her, forced her, and she took pepper poison and expired.
translations.idiomatic: " They seized her, forced the dose, and she died from the poison.

sentences.zh: 殯以后禮。

translations.literal: She was laid out with empress rites.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried with empress honors.

sentences.zh: 梓宮次洛南，咸陽王禧等知審死，相視曰：「若無遺詔，我兄弟亦當作計去之，豈可令失行婦人宰制天下，殺我輩也。

translations.literal: When the coffin halted south of Luoyang, Prince of Xianyang Xi and others learned she was truly dead and said to one another: "Without the testament we brothers would also have had to scheme to remove her—how could we let a woman of misconduct rule the realm and kill us?
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin paused south of Luoyang, Prince of Xianyang Xi and others learned she was dead and said to one another: "Without the testament we would have removed her ourselves—how could a disgraced woman rule the realm and destroy us?

sentences.zh: 」諡曰幽皇后，葬長陵塋內。

translations.literal: " Her posthumous title was Empress You, and she was buried within the precinct of Changling.
translations.idiomatic: " She was posthumously named Empress You and buried within Changling.

sentences.zh: 孝文昭皇后高氏，司徒公肇之妹也。

translations.literal: Empress Zhao of Emperor Wen, the Gao clan, was a younger sister of Duke of the State as Minister of Education Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhao of Emperor Wen, née Gao, was a sister of Minister of Education Zhao, Duke of the State.

sentences.zh: 父颺，母蓋氏，凡四男三女，皆生於東裔。

translations.literal: Her father Yang; her mother the Ge clan; in all four sons and three daughters, all born in the eastern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was Yang; her mother was of the Ge clan; they had four sons and three daughters, all born in the eastern marches.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，乃舉室西歸，達龍城鎮，鎮表后德色婉豔，任充宮掖。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's reign the whole family moved west; reaching Longcheng garrison, the garrison reported the empress's virtue, beauty, and gentle charm, fit to fill the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Gaozu's reign the family moved west; at Longcheng garrison the commandant reported her grace and beauty, fit for the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 及至，文明太后親幸北部曹，見后姿貌，奇之，遂入掖庭，時年十三。

translations.literal: When she arrived, Empress Dowager Wenming personally visited the northern bureau, saw the empress's looks, marveled, and had her enter the inner palace at age thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Empress Dowager Wenming visited the northern bureau herself, marveled at her looks, and sent her into the inner palace at thirteen.

sentences.zh: 初，后幼曾夢在堂內立，而日光自窗中照之，灼灼而熱，后東西避之，光猶斜照不已。

translations.literal: Earlier, when young, the empress once dreamed she stood in a hall while sunlight from the window shone on her, blazing hot; she dodged east and west, yet the light still slanted upon her without cease.
translations.idiomatic: As a girl she dreamed she stood in a hall while sunlight poured through the window, burning hot; she dodged east and west, but the light still found her.

sentences.zh: 如是數夕，后自怪之，以白其父颺，颺以問遼東人閔宗。

translations.literal: Thus for several nights; the empress thought it strange and told her father Yang; Yang asked Min Zong of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: For several nights she wondered at it and told her father Yang, who consulted Min Zong of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 宗曰：「此奇徵也，貴不可言。

translations.literal: Zong said: "This is a strange omen; nobility beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: Min Zong said: "This is a rare sign—honor beyond speech.

sentences.zh: 」颺曰：「何以知之？

translations.literal: " Yang said: "How do you know?
translations.idiomatic: " Yang asked: "How can you tell?

sentences.zh: 」宗曰：「夫日者，君人之德，帝王之象也。

translations.literal: " Zong said: "The sun is the virtue of a ruler, the image of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: " He said: "The sun is the ruler's virtue, the sign of sovereignty.

sentences.zh: 光照女身，必有恩命及之。

translations.literal: Light shining on a woman's body means favor and command will reach her.
translations.idiomatic: Light on a woman means imperial favor will find her.

sentences.zh: 女避猶照者，主上來求，女不獲已也。

translations.literal: That she dodged yet was still lit means the sovereign will come seeking her and she will have no choice.
translations.idiomatic: That she dodged yet was still lit means the lord will seek her and she cannot refuse.

sentences.zh: 昔有夢月入懷，猶生天子，況日照之徵。

translations.literal: In old times one dreamed the moon entered her womb and still bore a Son of Heaven—how much more a sign of sunlight.
translations.idiomatic: Once a woman dreamed the moon entered her womb and bore a Son of Heaven—how much more sunlight.

sentences.zh: 此女必將被帝命，誕育人君之象也。

translations.literal: This girl will surely receive the imperial mandate and bear the image of one who nurtures a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: This girl will receive the imperial mandate and bear a ruler of men.

sentences.zh: 」遂生世宗。

translations.literal: " She then bore Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: " She bore Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 後生廣平王懷，次長樂公主。

translations.literal: Later she bore Prince of Guangping Huai, then Princess Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Later she bore Prince of Guangping Huai, then Princess Changle.

sentences.zh: 及馮昭儀寵盛，密有母養世宗之意，后自代如洛陽，暴薨於汲郡之共縣，或云昭儀遣人賊后也。

translations.literal: When Lady Feng the zhaoyi's favor flourished, she secretly intended to mother and raise Xuanzong; the empress went herself to Luoyang and suddenly died at Gong county in Ji commandery—some say the zhaoyi sent men to assassinate the empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng the zhaoyi rose in favor and plotted to raise Xuanzong as her own, the empress went to Luoyang and died suddenly at Gong in Ji commandery—some said the zhaoyi had her murdered.

sentences.zh: 世宗之為皇太子，三日一朝幽后，后拊念慈愛有加。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was crown prince he attended Empress You every three days; she caressed and remembered him with added motherly love.
translations.idiomatic: As crown prince Xuanzong visited Empress You every three days; she doted on him with growing affection.

sentences.zh: 高祖出征，世宗入朝，必久留后宮，親視櫛沐，母道隆備。

translations.literal: When Gaozu campaigned, Xuanzong entering court always stayed long in the inner palace; she personally watched his combing and bathing—motherly conduct in full measure.
translations.idiomatic: On Gaozu's campaigns Xuanzong would linger in the inner palace, where she personally attended his grooming—her motherhood complete.

sentences.zh: 其後有司奏請加昭儀號，諡曰文昭貴人，高祖從之。

translations.literal: Later the authorities memorialized to add the zhaoyi title; her posthumous name was Worthy Lady Wenzhao, and Gaozu assented.
translations.idiomatic: Later officials petitioned to grant her the zhaoyi title posthumously as Worthy Lady Wenzhao, and Gaozu agreed.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，追尊配饗。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, she was honored posthumously with joint offerings.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne, she was posthumously honored with joint temple sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 后先葬城西長陵東南，陵制卑局。

translations.literal: The empress had first been buried southeast of Changling outside the western city; the tomb precinct was low and cramped.
translations.idiomatic: She had first been buried southeast of Changling outside the west wall, in a modest tomb layout.

sentences.zh: 因就起山陵，號終寧陵，置邑戶五百家。

translations.literal: A hill tomb was therefore raised on the spot, named Zhongning Mausoleum, with five hundred householders for the fief.
translations.idiomatic: A hill tomb was raised there, named Zhongning Mausoleum, with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 肅宗詔曰：「文昭皇太后，德協坤儀，美符文姒，作合高祖，實誕英聖，而夙世淪暉，孤塋弗祔。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong edicted: "Grand Empress Dowager Wenzhao—her virtue matched earth's measure, her beauty echoed Wen Jiang; united with Gaozu she truly bore a sage, yet her early death dimmed her light and her lonely mound was not joined.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong decreed: "Grand Empress Dowager Wenzhao matched earth in virtue and Wen Jiang in grace; wed to Gaozu she bore a sage, yet she died young and her lonely mound was not joined in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 先帝孝感自衷，遷奉未遂，永言哀恨，義結幽明。

translations.literal: The late emperor's filial feeling came from the heart; the transfer of her remains was not completed—endless grief and resentment, righteousness binding the hidden and the bright.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's filial heart could not finish moving her; grief binds the living and the dead.

sentences.zh: 廢呂尊薄，禮伸漢代。

translations.literal: Deposing Lü and honoring Bo, the rites of Han were fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: As Han deposed Lü and honored Bo, so shall rite be restored.

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「文昭皇太后尊配高祖，祔廟定號，促令遷奉，自終及始，太后當主，可更上尊號稱太皇太后，以同漢晉之典，正姑婦之禮。

translations.literal: " Another edict said: "Grand Empress Dowager Wenzhao, honored with Gaozu, enshrined in the temple with title fixed—hasten the transfer of her remains; from end to beginning the empress dowager shall preside. She may further be elevated to Grand Empress Dowager, matching Han and Jin precedent and rectifying mother-in-law and daughter-in-law rites.
translations.idiomatic: " A second decree said: "Grand Empress Dowager Wenzhao is to be honored with Gaozu, enshrined, and moved at once; from first to last the empress dowager shall preside. Raise her title to Grand Empress Dowager, as in Han and Jin, to set mother-in-law and daughter-in-law rites aright.

sentences.zh: 廟號如舊。

translations.literal: Her temple title remains as before.
translations.idiomatic: Her temple title remains unchanged.

sentences.zh: 」文昭遷靈櫬於長陵兆西北六十步。

translations.literal: " Wenzhao's spirit coffin was moved sixty paces northwest of Changling's precinct.
translations.idiomatic: " Her coffin was moved sixty paces northwest of Changling's mound.

sentences.zh: 初開終寧陵數丈，於梓宮上獲大蛇長丈餘，黑色，頭有「王」字，蟄而不動。

translations.literal: When Zhongning Mausoleum was first opened several zhang deep, on the outer coffin a great serpent more than a zhang long was found, black, with the character "king" on its head, coiled and motionless.
translations.idiomatic: When the tomb was opened several zhang deep, a black serpent over a zhang long was found on the coffin, the character "king" on its head, coiled and still.

sentences.zh: 靈櫬既遷，置蛇舊處。

translations.literal: After the spirit coffin was moved, the serpent was placed back in its former spot.
translations.idiomatic: After the move the serpent was returned to its place.

sentences.zh: 宣武順皇后于氏，太尉烈弟勁之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Shun of Emperor Xuanwu, the Yu clan, was a daughter of Lie's younger brother Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shun of Emperor Xuanwu, née Yu, was a daughter of Jin, younger brother of Grand Commandant Lie.

sentences.zh: 世宗始親政事，烈時為領軍，總心膂之任，以嬪御未備，因左右諷諭，稱后有容德，世宗乃迎入為貴人。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong first personally handled government, Lie was then director of the guards, holding the core trust; as consorts were not yet complete, through attendants' persuasion they praised the empress's looks and virtue, and Xuanzong welcomed her in as noble lady.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong began to rule in person, Lie commanded the guards; attendants praised the empress's grace, and Xuanzong took her in as a noble lady.

sentences.zh: 時年十四，甚見寵愛，立為皇后，謁于太廟。

translations.literal: She was fourteen, greatly favored, installed as empress, and presented at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen she was deeply favored, made empress, and presented at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 后靜默寬容，性不妬忌，生皇子昌，三歲夭歿。

translations.literal: The empress was quiet, forbearing, and not jealous; she bore Prince Chang, who died at three.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and tolerant, not jealous, she bore Prince Chang, who died at three.

sentences.zh: 其後暴崩，宮禁事祕，莫能知悉，而世議歸咎于高夫人。

translations.literal: Later she died suddenly; palace affairs were secret and none could know fully, yet public opinion blamed Lady Gao.
translations.idiomatic: She then died suddenly; palace matters were secret, but opinion blamed Lady Gao.

sentences.zh: 葬永泰陵，諡曰順皇后。

translations.literal: She was buried at Yongtai Mausoleum with posthumous title Empress Shun.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried at Yongtai Mausoleum as Empress Shun.

sentences.zh: 宣武皇后高氏，文昭皇后弟偃之女也。

translations.literal: Empress of Emperor Xuanwu, the Gao clan, was a daughter of Wenzhao Empress's younger brother Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress of Emperor Xuanwu, née Gao, was a daughter of Wenzhao Empress's brother Yan.

sentences.zh: 世宗納為貴人，生皇子，早夭，又生建德公主。

translations.literal: Xuanzong took her in as noble lady; she bore a prince who died young, and also Princess Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong took her as noble lady; a prince died young, then she bore Princess Jiande.

sentences.zh: 後拜為皇后，甚見禮重。

translations.literal: Later she was appointed empress and was greatly honored.
translations.idiomatic: She was later made empress and held in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 性妬忌，宮人希得進御。

translations.literal: By nature jealous, palace women rarely gained access to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous by nature, she kept other women from the emperor's bed.

sentences.zh: 及肅宗即位，上尊號曰皇太后。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, she was given the exalted title Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong took the throne she was made empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 尋為尼，居瑤光寺，非大節慶，不入宮中。

translations.literal: Soon she became a nun, dwelling at Yaoguang Temple; except for great festivals she did not enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: She soon took the veil at Yaoguang Temple and entered the palace only on great occasions.

sentences.zh: 建德公主始五六歲，靈太后恒置左右，撫愛之。

translations.literal: Princess Jiande, only five or six, Empress Dowager Ling always kept at her side and cherished her.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jiande, five or six years old, Empress Dowager Ling kept always beside her and cherished her.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年，太后出覲母武邑君。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengui the empress dowager went out to visit her mother Lady of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengui year 1 the empress dowager went to visit her mother, Lady of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 時天文有變，靈太后欲以后當禍，是夜暴崩，天下冤之。

translations.literal: Heavenly signs were then in flux; Empress Dowager Ling wished the empress to bear the calamity; that night she died suddenly, and the realm deemed it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Omens were abroad; Empress Dowager Ling meant the empress to take the blame; that night she died suddenly, and the realm cried injustice.

sentences.zh: 喪還瑤光佛寺，嬪葬皆以尼禮。

translations.literal: The funeral returned to Yaoguang Buddhist Temple; burial of consorts all followed nun rites.
translations.idiomatic: Her funeral was at Yaoguang Temple, with nun rites as for a consort.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖幽后之寵也，欲專其愛，後宮接御，多見阻遏。

translations.literal: At first, during Gaozu's favor for Empress You, he wished to keep his love exclusive; access in the inner palace was often blocked.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu favored Empress You he sought exclusive love and often barred the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 高祖時言于近臣，稱婦人妬防，雖王者亦不能免，況士庶乎？

translations.literal: Gaozu once told close ministers that women's jealousy and guarding—even kings cannot escape it, how much more commoners?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu once told his intimates that even kings cannot escape a woman's jealousy—how much less common men?

sentences.zh: 世宗暮年，高后悍忌，夫人嬪御有至帝崩不蒙侍接者。

translations.literal: In Xuanzong's later years Empress Gao was fierce and jealous; ladies and concubines included some who until the emperor's death never received him.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanzong's last years Empress Gao was fierce; some consorts never saw the emperor until his death.

sentences.zh: 由是在洛二世，二十餘年，皇子全育者，惟肅宗而已。

translations.literal: Thus in two reigns at Luoyang, for more than twenty years, the only prince raised whole was Xiaozong alone.
translations.idiomatic: Thus through two reigns at Luoyang, for over twenty years, only Xiaozong among princes was raised to adulthood.

sentences.zh: 宣武靈皇后胡氏，安定臨涇人，司徒國珍女也。

translations.literal: Empress Ling of Emperor Xuanwu, the Hu clan, was a native of Linjing in Anding, daughter of Minister of Education Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ling of Emperor Xuanwu, née Hu, came from Linjing in Anding, daughter of Minister of Education Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 母皇甫氏，產后之日，赤光四照。

translations.literal: Her mother was the Huangfu clan; on the day the empress was born, red light shone on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was of the Huangfu clan; on her birth day red light filled the room.

sentences.zh: 京兆山北縣有趙胡者，善於卜相，國珍問之。

translations.literal: In Shangbei county of Jingzhao there was Zhao Hu, skilled in divination and physiognomy; Guozhen questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hu of Shangbei in Jingzhao, skilled in divination, was consulted by Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 胡云：「賢女有大貴之表，方為天地母，生天地主。

translations.literal: Hu said: "Your worthy daughter bears the marks of great nobility; she will become mother of heaven and earth and bear the lord of heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Hu said: "This worthy daughter shows supreme nobility; she will be mother of the realm and bear its lord.

sentences.zh: 勿過三人知也。

translations.literal: Let no more than three persons know.
translations.idiomatic: Let no more than three know of this.

sentences.zh: 」后姑為尼，頗能講道，世宗初，入講禁中。

translations.literal: " The empress's aunt was a nun, quite able to expound the Way; at the beginning of Xuanzong's reign she entered the forbidden precinct to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Her aunt was a nun skilled in doctrine who entered the palace early in Xuanzong's reign to lecture.

sentences.zh: 積數歲，諷左右稱后姿行，世宗聞之，乃召入掖庭為承華世婦。

translations.literal: After several years attendants were prompted to praise the empress's looks and conduct; Xuanzong heard and summoned her to the inner palace as Shining Splendor world-lady.
translations.idiomatic: For years attendants praised her grace; Xuanzong heard and summoned her to the inner palace as Shining Splendor attendant.

sentences.zh: 而椒掖之中，以國舊制，相與祈祝，皆願生諸王、公主，不願生太子。

translations.literal: Yet in the pepper chambers, by the state's old custom, they prayed together, all wishing to bear princes and princesses, not wishing to bear the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom women of the inner palace prayed together to bear princes or princesses, not the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 唯后每謂夫人等言：「天子豈可獨無兒子，何緣畏一身之死而令皇家不育冢嫡乎？

translations.literal: Only the empress often told the ladies: "Can the Son of Heaven truly have no son? Why fear one's own death and leave the imperial house without its legitimate heir?
translations.idiomatic: Only she told the ladies: "Can the Son of Heaven have no son? Why fear death and leave the house without its heir?

sentences.zh: 」及肅宗在孕，同列猶以故事相恐，勸為諸計。

translations.literal: " When Xiaozong was in her womb, her peers still frightened her with precedent and urged various schemes.
translations.idiomatic: " When she carried Xiaozong, her peers still frightened her with precedent and urged schemes against it.

sentences.zh: 后固意確然，幽夜獨誓云：「但使所懷是男，次第當長子，子生身死，所不辭也。

translations.literal: The empress's resolve was firm; in the dark night she vowed alone: "If what I carry is a boy and by order he should be eldest son, though bearing him costs my life I will not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: She was resolute; in the dark she vowed alone: "If it is a boy and he is to be heir, I accept death in giving birth.

sentences.zh: 」既誕肅宗，進為充華嬪。

translations.literal: " After Xiaozong was born she was advanced to Full Splendor concubine.
translations.idiomatic: " After Xiaozong was born she was made Full Splendor concubine.

sentences.zh: 先是，世宗頻喪皇子，自以春秋長矣，深加慎護。

translations.literal: Before this Xuanzong had frequently lost princes; considering himself advanced in years, he guarded them deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had lost many sons; feeling his years advance, he guarded infants strictly.

sentences.zh: 為擇乳保，皆取良家宜子者。

translations.literal: Wet nurses were chosen, all from good families suited to bear sons.
translations.idiomatic: He chose wet nurses from good families known for bearing sons.

sentences.zh: 養於別宮，皇后及充華嬪皆莫得而撫視焉。

translations.literal: They were raised in a separate palace; neither the empress nor the Full Splendor concubine might nurse or see them.
translations.idiomatic: They were reared in a separate palace; neither empress nor concubine might rear or see them.

sentences.zh: 及肅宗踐阼，尊后為皇太妃，後尊為皇太后。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, she was first honored as imperial consort dowager, then as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong took the throne she was first grand imperial consort, then empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 臨朝聽政，猶稱殿下，下令行事。

translations.literal: She held court and heard government, still styled "Your Highness" below the throne, and issued orders to conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: She held court, still addressed as "Your Highness," and issued orders.

sentences.zh: 後改令稱詔，羣臣上書曰陛下，自稱曰朕。

translations.literal: Later orders were styled edicts; ministers' memorials addressed her as "Your Majesty," and she called herself "I, the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Later her orders were called edicts; ministers wrote "Your Majesty," and she used "I."

sentences.zh: 太后以肅宗沖幼，未堪親祭，欲傍周禮夫人與君交獻之義，代行祭禮，訪尋故式。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, because Xiaozong was young and not yet able to sacrifice in person, wished to follow Zhou ritual's meaning of wife and lord mutually offering sacrifice and perform the rites in his stead, seeking former precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiaozong was too young to sacrifice, she sought Zhou precedent for the consort's shared offering and meant to perform the rites herself.

sentences.zh: 門下召禮官、博士議，以為不可。

translations.literal: The Secretariat summoned ritual officers and academicians to debate; they deemed it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat summoned ritualists and scholars, who ruled it impossible.

sentences.zh: 而太后欲以幃幔自鄣，觀三公行事，重問侍中崔光。

translations.literal: Yet the empress dowager wished to screen herself with curtains and observe the Three Excellencies performing the rites, and questioned Attendant-in-ordinary Cui Guang again.
translations.idiomatic: She wished to watch from behind a curtain as the Three Excellencies performed the rites and questioned Attendant-in-ordinary Cui Guang again.

sentences.zh: 光便據漢和熹鄧后薦祭故事，太后大悅，遂攝行初祀。

translations.literal: Guang promptly cited the Han precedent of Empress Dowager He and Xi of Deng recommending sacrifice; the empress dowager was greatly pleased and then acted in place for the first sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Guang cited Empress Dowager Deng of Han; delighted, she performed the first sacrifice in the emperor's stead.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 太后性聰悟，多才藝，姑既為尼，幼相依託，略得佛經大義。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was clever and perceptive, with many talents; her aunt being a nun, they relied on each other from childhood and she grasped the great meaning of Buddhist sutras.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and gifted, she had been raised by her nun aunt and grasped the gist of the sutras.

sentences.zh: 親覽萬機，手筆斷決。

translations.literal: She personally reviewed the myriad affairs of state and decided with her own hand.
translations.idiomatic: She personally reviewed state affairs and wrote judgments herself.

sentences.zh: 幸西林園法流堂，命侍臣射，不能者罰之。

translations.literal: Visiting the Faliu Hall in Xilin Garden, she ordered attendant ministers to shoot; those who could not were punished.
translations.idiomatic: At Faliu Hall in Xilin Garden she ordered ministers to shoot; failures were punished.

sentences.zh: 又自射針孔，中之。

translations.literal: She herself shot at a needle's eye and hit it.
translations.idiomatic: She herself shot at a needle's eye and struck true.

sentences.zh: 大悅，賜左右布帛有差。

translations.literal: Greatly pleased, she bestowed cloth and silk on those around her in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, she gave graded gifts of cloth and silk to those around her.

sentences.zh: 先是，太后敕造申訟車，時御焉，出自雲龍大司馬門，從宮西北，入自千秋門，以納冤訟。

translations.literal: Earlier the empress dowager had ordered the construction of a petition carriage; she now rode it, going out from the Cloud Dragon grand marshal gate, circling northwest of the palace, entering by the Thousand Autumns gate to receive wrongful grievances.
translations.idiomatic: She had built a petition carriage and rode it out the Cloud Dragon gate, around the palace's northwest, in by the Thousand Autumns gate to hear grievances.

sentences.zh: 又親策孝秀、州郡計吏於朝堂。

translations.literal: She also personally examined filial scholars and outstanding men and the commandery and district clerks at court.
translations.idiomatic: She also examined filial scholars and provincial clerks in the hall of audience.

sentences.zh: 太后與肅宗幸華林園，宴羣臣于都亭曲水，令王公已下各賦七言詩。

translations.literal: The empress dowager and Xiaozong visited Hualin Garden, feasted the ministers at the winding water of the capital pavilion, and ordered princes, dukes, and below each to compose a seven-character verse poem.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiaozong at Hualin Garden she feasted ministers at the winding stream and ordered each prince and official to compose a heptasyllabic poem.

sentences.zh: 太后詩曰：「化光造物含氣貞。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's poem said: "Transforming light creates things; holding qi, steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: Her poem ran: "Transforming light creates things; holding breath, steadfast."

sentences.zh: 」帝詩曰：「恭己無為賴慈英。

translations.literal: " The emperor's poem said: "Respectfully restraining myself, inactive—I rely on kind excellence.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's: "Respectfully at rest, I rely on kind excellence."

sentences.zh: 」王公已下賜帛有差。

translations.literal: " Princes, dukes, and below received graded gifts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: " Princes and officials below received graded gifts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 太后父薨，百僚表請公除，太后不許。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's father died; the hundred officials memorialized requesting she leave office for mourning; the empress dowager did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When her father died officials asked her to observe mourning; she refused.

sentences.zh: 尋幸永寧寺，親建剎於九級之基，僧尼士女赴者數萬人。

translations.literal: Soon she visited Yongning Temple and personally built a shrine on a nine-tier foundation; monks, nuns, gentlemen, and ladies who came numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: She visited Yongning Temple and built a shrine on a nine-tier base; tens of thousands of clergy and layfolk came.

sentences.zh: 及改葬文昭高后，太后不欲令肅宗主事，乃自為喪主，出至終寧陵，親奠遣事，還哭於太極殿，至於訖事，皆自主焉。

translations.literal: When Wenzhao Empress Gao was reburied, the empress dowager did not wish Xiaozong to preside; she herself became chief mourner, went out to Zhongning Mausoleum, personally offered the farewell rites, returned to weep at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and through completion presided over all.
translations.idiomatic: At Wenzhao Empress Gao's reburial she would not let Xiaozong preside; she went to Zhongning as chief mourner, offered rites, wept at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and directed everything.

sentences.zh: 後幸嵩高山，夫人、九嬪、公主已下從者數百人，昇于頂中。

translations.literal: Later she visited Mount Song; ladies, the nine concubines, princesses, and those below who followed numbered several hundred, ascending to the summit.
translations.idiomatic: Later she climbed Mount Song with hundreds of consorts and princesses to the summit.

sentences.zh: 廢諸淫祀，而胡天神不在其列。

translations.literal: She abolished various licentious sacrifices, but the Hu heavenly god was not among them.
translations.idiomatic: She abolished illicit shrines but exempted the Hu heavenly cult.

sentences.zh: 後幸左藏，王公、嬪、主已下從者百餘人，皆令任力負布絹，即以賜之，多者過二百匹，少者百餘匹。

translations.literal: Later she visited the left treasury; princes, dukes, consorts, princesses, and those below who followed numbered more than a hundred—all were made to carry cloth and silk by their strength, then rewarded with it; the most received over two hundred bolts, the least more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At the left treasury she made over a hundred princes and ladies carry cloth and silk by strength, then gave it back—some over two hundred bolts, some over a hundred.

sentences.zh: 唯長樂公主手持絹二十匹而出，示不異眾而無勞也。

translations.literal: Only Princess Changle came out holding twenty bolts of silk in her hands, showing she was not different from the crowd yet without toil.
translations.idiomatic: Only Princess Changle carried out twenty bolts by hand, showing she matched the crowd without strain.

sentences.zh: 世稱其廉。

translations.literal: The age praised her frugality.
translations.idiomatic: The age praised her restraint.

sentences.zh: 儀同、陳留公李崇，章武王融並以所負過多，顛仆於地，崇乃傷腰，融至損脚。

translations.literal: Equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, Duke of Chenliu Li Chong, and Prince of Zhangwu Rong both from carrying too much fell to the ground; Chong injured his waist, Rong even damaged his foot.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, Duke of Chenliu, and Prince of Zhangwu Rong, bearing too much, fell—Chong hurt his back, Rong his leg.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「陳留、章武，傷腰折股。

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying: "Chenliu and Zhangwu—hurt waist, broken thigh.
translations.idiomatic: A rhyme ran: "Chenliu and Zhangwu—hurt back, broken leg.

sentences.zh: 貪人敗類，穢我明主。

translations.literal: Greedy men ruin their kind and defile our enlightened lord.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy men shame our bright sovereign."

sentences.zh: 」尋幸闕口溫水，登鷄頭山，自射象牙簪，一發中之，敕示文武。

translations.literal: " Soon she visited the warm springs at Quekou, climbed Chicken Head Mountain, shot at an ivory hairpin herself, hit it with one shot, and ordered it shown to civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: " She visited Quekou hot springs, climbed Chicken Head Mountain, shot an ivory hairpin at one cast, and displayed it to the court.

sentences.zh: 時太后得志，逼幸清河王懌，淫亂肆情，為天下所惡。

translations.literal: By then the empress dowager had her will; she forced her favor on Prince of Qinghe Yi and indulged in lewd disorder at will, hated by the realm.
translations.idiomatic: By then she forced herself on Prince of Qinghe Yi and indulged openly, hated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 領軍元叉、長秋卿劉騰等奉肅宗於顯陽殿，幽太后於北宮，於禁中殺懌。

translations.literal: Director of the guards Yuan Cha, Director of the Long Autumn Liu Teng, and others installed Xiaozong in Xianyang Hall, confined the empress dowager in the northern palace, and killed Yi within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha and Liu Teng installed Xiaozong in Xianyang Hall, confined her in the northern palace, and killed Yi inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 其後太后從子都統僧敬與備身左右張車渠等數十人，謀殺叉，復奉太后臨朝，事不克，僧敬坐徙邊，車渠等死，胡氏多免黜。

translations.literal: Later the empress dowager's cousin Colonel-in-chief Sengjing and several dozen bodyguards including Zhang Chequ plotted to kill Cha and restore the empress dowager to court; it failed—Sengjing was banished to the frontier, Chequ and others died, and many of the Hu clan were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Her cousin Sengjing and dozens of guards plotted to kill Cha and restore her; it failed—Sengjing was exiled, Chequ executed, many Hus dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後肅宗朝太后於西林園，讌文武侍臣，飲至日夕。

translations.literal: Later Xiaozong attended the empress dowager at Xilin Garden, feasted civil and military attendant ministers, and drank until evening.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiaozong visited her at Xilin Garden and feasted ministers until evening.

sentences.zh: 叉乃起至太后前，自陳外云太后欲害己及騰。

translations.literal: Cha then rose before the empress dowager and, speaking outward, claimed the empress dowager wished to harm him and Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Cha rose before her and declared aloud that she meant to kill him and Teng.

sentences.zh: 太后答云「無此語」。

translations.literal: The empress dowager answered that there was no such talk.
translations.idiomatic: She answered that she had said no such thing.

sentences.zh: 遂至于極昏。

translations.literal: It then reached extreme confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Matters descended into utter chaos.

sentences.zh: 太后乃起執肅宗手下堂，言：「母子不聚久，今暮共一宿，諸大臣送我入。

translations.literal: The empress dowager then rose, took Xiaozong's hand, and left the hall, saying: "Mother and son have not gathered long; tonight we shall lodge together—ministers, escort me in.
translations.idiomatic: She took Xiaozong's hand and left, saying: "Mother and son have been apart too long—we lodge together tonight; ministers, see me in.

sentences.zh: 」太后與肅宗向東北小閤，左衞將軍奚康生謀欲殺叉，不果。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager and Xiaozong went to a small chamber in the northeast; Left Guard General Xi Kangsheng plotted to kill Cha but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: " They went to a northeast chamber; Left Guard General Xi Kangsheng plotted to kill Cha but failed.

sentences.zh: 自劉騰死，叉又寬怠。

translations.literal: After Liu Teng died, Cha again grew lax and negligent.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Teng's death Cha grew lax again.

sentences.zh: 太后與肅宗及高陽王雍為計，解叉領軍。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, Xiaozong, and Prince of Gaoyang Yong plotted together and removed Cha from the directorship of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: She, Xiaozong, and Prince of Gaoyang Yong plotted and stripped Cha of the guards command.

sentences.zh: 太后復臨朝，大赦改元。

translations.literal: The empress dowager again held court, proclaimed a great amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: She returned to court, proclaimed a great amnesty, and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 自是朝政疏緩，威恩不立，天下牧守，所在貪惏。

translations.literal: From then government grew slack, authority and favor were not established, and prefects and shepherds everywhere were greedy.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter government slackened, authority waned, and local officials grew greedy everywhere.

sentences.zh: 鄭儼汙亂宮掖，勢傾海內；

translations.literal: Zheng Yan defiled the inner palace; his power tilted the seas within.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yan defiled the inner palace and his power tilted the realm;

sentences.zh: 李神軌、徐紇並見親侍。

translations.literal: Li Shengui and Xu He were both received in close attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shengui and Xu He enjoyed intimate attendance.

sentences.zh: 一二年中，位總禁要，手握王爵，輕重在心，宣淫於朝，為四方之所厭穢。

translations.literal: Within a year or two they held posts summing the forbidden core, grasped princely seals in their hands, weight and lightness lay in their hearts, proclaimed lewdness at court, and were loathed and defiled by the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year or two they held the palace's keys, grasped princely seals, ruled by whim, flaunted lust at court, and were loathed in every quarter.

sentences.zh: 文武解體，所在亂逆，土崩魚爛，由於此矣。

translations.literal: Civil and military offices dissolved; rebellion rose everywhere—earth collapsing, fish rotting—from this it came.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military order collapsed, rebellion spread everywhere—the realm crumbled from this.

sentences.zh: 僧敬又因聚集親族，遂涕泣諫曰：「陛下母儀海內，豈宜輕脫如此！

translations.literal: Sengjing again, gathering kin, wept and remonstrated: "Your Majesty, motherly model of the seas within—how can you cast restraint aside so lightly!
translations.idiomatic: Sengjing gathered kin and wept in remonstrance: "Your Majesty, model of motherhood for the realm—how can you cast restraint aside so lightly!

sentences.zh: 」后大怒，自是不召僧敬。

translations.literal: " The empress was greatly angry and from then did not summon Sengjing.
translations.idiomatic: " She flew into a rage and never summoned Sengjing again.

sentences.zh: 太后自以行不修，懼宗室所嫌，於是內為朋黨，防蔽耳目，肅宗所親幸者，太后多以事害焉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, considering her conduct unreformed, feared resentment from the imperial clan; she therefore formed factions within, blocked ears and eyes, and many whom Xiaozong favored the empress dowager harmed on one pretext or another.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing her conduct was shameful and fearing the clan, she formed factions, sealed off news, and destroyed many Xiaozong favored.

sentences.zh: 有蜜多道人，能胡語，肅宗置於左右。

translations.literal: There was a Daoist named Mituo who could speak barbarian tongues; Emperor Suzong kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist called Mituo, fluent in the northern languages, served at Emperor Suzong's elbow.

sentences.zh: 太后慮其傳致消息，三月三日於城南大巷中殺之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager feared he would carry messages; on the third day of the third month she had him killed in the great south-city lane.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he might pass intelligence, the Dowager had him slain in the main south-city street on the third day of the third month.

sentences.zh: 方懸賞募賊，又於禁中殺領左右、鴻臚少卿谷會、紹達，並帝所親也。

translations.literal: While rewards were posted to recruit the assassins, in the inner palace she also killed the Directors of the Left and Right Guard, Director of the Palace Secretariat Gu Hui, and Shaoda—all men the emperor favored.
translations.idiomatic: Bounties were still out for the killers when she struck again inside the palace, executing the guard directors, Gu Hui of the Palace Secretariat, and Shaoda, each a favorite of the throne.

sentences.zh: 母子之間，嫌隙屢起。

translations.literal: Between mother and son, suspicion and rifts arose repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and son nursed grievance after grievance.

sentences.zh: 鄭儼慮禍，乃與太后計，因潘充華生女，太后詐以為男，便大赦改年。

translations.literal: Zheng Yan, fearing disaster, joined the Empress Dowager in a plot: when Lady Pan the Beautiful bore a daughter, the Dowager falsely announced a son, then proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign era.
translations.idiomatic: Dreading ruin, Zheng Yan conspired with the Dowager: when Lady Pan bore a girl, she was passed off as a boy, a great amnesty was declared, and the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 肅宗之崩，事出倉卒，時論咸言鄭儼、徐紇之計。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong's death came suddenly; contemporary opinion unanimously blamed the schemes of Zheng Yan and Xu He.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong's end was abrupt; everyone said Zheng Yan and Xu He had engineered it.

sentences.zh: 於是朝野憤歎。

translations.literal: Court and countryside alike groaned in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Grief and outrage spread through court and realm.

sentences.zh: 太后乃奉潘嬪女言太子即位。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then presented Lady Pan's daughter, saying the crown prince had ascended.
translations.idiomatic: The Dowager then installed Lady Pan's daughter, announcing that the heir had taken the throne.

sentences.zh: 經數日，見人心已安，始言潘嬪本實生女，今宜更擇嗣君。

translations.literal: After several days, seeing hearts had settled, she declared that Lady Pan had in fact borne a daughter and that a successor must now be chosen anew.
translations.idiomatic: When she judged opinion had calmed, she admitted the child was a girl and said a new heir must be chosen.

sentences.zh: 遂立臨洮王子釗為主，年始三歲，天下愕然。

translations.literal: They then installed Zhao, son of the Prince of Lin Tao, as ruler—he was just three years old—and the realm was stunned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, the Lin Tao prince's three-year-old son, was enthroned, and the empire reeled.

sentences.zh: 孝明皇后胡氏，靈太后從兄冀州刺史盛之女。

translations.literal: Empress Hu, consort of Emperor Xiaoming, was daughter of Sheng, governor of Jizhou and cousin of Empress Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Hu of Emperor Xiaoming was the daughter of Sheng, Jizhou governor and a cousin of Empress Ling.

sentences.zh: 靈太后欲榮重門族，故立為皇后。

translations.literal: Empress Ling wished to honor her clan, so she had her made empress.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ling meant to exalt her house and had her raised to the throne.

sentences.zh: 肅宗頗有酒德，專嬖充華潘氏，后及嬪御並無過寵。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong had a penchant for wine and favored exclusively Lady Pan the Beautiful; the empress and other consorts received no undue favor.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong drank heavily and doted only on Lady Pan; neither the empress nor the other ladies won special favor.

sentences.zh: 太后為肅宗選納，抑屈人流。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager selected consorts for Suzong and suppressed those who sought advancement.
translations.idiomatic: The Dowager chose his women herself and crushed anyone who pushed for rank.

sentences.zh: 時博陵崔孝芬、范陽盧道約、隴西李瓚等女，但為世婦。

translations.literal: At the time the daughters of Cui Xiaofen of Boling, Lu Daoyue of Fanyang, Li Zan of Longxi, and others were made only palace women of lower rank.
translations.idiomatic: Daughters of families such as Cui Xiaofen of Boling, Lu Daoyue of Fanyang, and Li Zan of Longxi were kept merely as palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 諸人訴訟，咸見忿責。

translations.literal: Those who petitioned in lawsuit all met with angry rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who sued for better treatment was berated in fury.

sentences.zh: 武泰初，后既入道，遂居於瑤光寺。

translations.literal: At the start of Wutai, after the empress took the tonsure, she resided at Yaoguang Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Wutai began she entered religion and lived at Yaoguang Temple.

sentences.zh: 孝靜皇后高氏，齊獻武王之第二女也。

translations.literal: Empress Gao, consort of Emperor Xiaojing, was the second daughter of King Xianwu of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gao of Emperor Xiaojing was the second daughter of Qi’s King Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 天平四年，詔娉以為皇后，王前後固辭，帝不許。

translations.literal: In Tianping year 4 an edict betrothed her as empress; the king repeatedly declined, but the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year 4 she was summoned as empress; the king refused again and again, but the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 興和初，詔侍中、司徒公孫騰，司空公、襄城王旭，兼尚書令、司州牧、西河王悰，兼太常卿及宗正卿元孝友等奉詔致禮，并備宮官侍衞，以后駕迎於晉陽之丞相第。

translations.literal: At the start of Xinghe, edicts ordered Chamberlain Sun Teng, Minister of Works Prince of Xiangcheng Xu, concurrently Director of the Department of State Affairs and Governor of Sizhou Prince of Xihe Cong, acting Director of Imperial Sacrifices and Director of Imperial Clansmen Yuan Xiaoyou and others to perform the rites and equip palace officials and guards; the empress was escorted by carriage from the chancellor's mansion at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xinghe, Sun Teng as chamberlain, Prince Xu of Xiangcheng as minister of works, Prince Cong of Xihe as acting director of the secretariat and Sizhou governor, Yuan Xiaoyou as acting director of sacrifices and director of clansmen, and others were charged to conduct the rites, furnish palace staff and guards, and bring the empress by carriage from the chancellor’s house at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 五月，立為皇后，大赦天下。

translations.literal: In the fifth month she was installed as empress and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month she was crowned and the realm was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，降為中山王妃。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication she was demoted to Princess of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took the mandate she became Princess of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 後降于尚書左僕射楊遵彥。

translations.literal: Later she married down to Yang Zunyan, Left Vice-Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: She later wed Yang Zunyan, left vice-director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：始祖生自天女，克昌後葉。

translations.literal: The historian says: The founding ancestor was born of a celestial maiden and his line flourished afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The founder sprang from a heaven-sent maiden, and his house prospered for generations.

sentences.zh: 靈后淫恣，卒亡天下。

translations.literal: Empress Ling was licentious and willful; she ultimately lost the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ling gave way to lust and arrogance and in the end lost the empire.

sentences.zh: 傾城之戒，其在茲乎？

translations.literal: Is this not where the warning against women who topple states applies?
translations.idiomatic: Was the lesson of cities laid waste not written here?

sentences.zh: 鈎弋年稚子幼，漢武所以行權，魏世遂為常制。

translations.literal: Gouyi was young when her son was young; Emperor Wu of Han therefore acted expediently, and in Wei times it became regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gouyi was still a child when her son was an infant; Han Wudi seized that moment as expedient policy, and under Wei it hardened into custom.

sentences.zh: 子貴母死，矯枉之義不亦過哉！

translations.literal: When the son is honored the mother dies—is not the corrective overdone!
translations.idiomatic: Honor the son, kill the mother—has the remedy not swung too far?

sentences.zh: 高祖終革其失，良有以也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu finally abolished this abuse; he had good reason.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu at last swept the abuse away, and rightly so.

translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

translations.literal: Wei shu juan 13: Various editions' tables of contents mark this juan "deficient." The Baipu, Nan, Ji, and Ju editions all have Song-dynasty collation notes at the end of the juan stating: "The Wei shu biographies of empresses are lost; later persons supplemented them from the Beishi, and also added material from the Gaoshi xiaoshi and the Xiufen dian yulan."
translations.idiomatic: Wei shu juan 13: In several editions the table of contents labels this scroll "lacunose." Baipu, Nan, Ji, and Ju copies alike carry a Song note at the juan’s end: the empress chapters of Wei Shou’s original are missing; later editors patched them from Beishi and padded them with Gaoshi xiaoshi and Xiufen dian yulan.

sentences.zh: 」殿本入考證，止云：「魏收書亡，後人所補。」

translations.literal: " The Dian edition places this in Kaozheng and only says: "The Wei shu is lost; later persons supplemented it."
translations.idiomatic: " The Dian edition tucks the matter into Kaozheng and merely says, "Wei Shou’s text is gone; what follows is later supplementation."

translations.idiomatic: Equivalent to fifth rank. These inner-palace offices lack corroboration elsewhere; the breaks are editorial guesses.

translations.literal: "Spring Robes," Beishi juan 13, Biographies of Empresses and Consorts, reads "Green Robes."
translations.idiomatic: "Spring Robes" appears as "Green Robes" in Beishi juan 13 (Empresses and Consorts).

sentences.zh: 是非無從判斷。

translations.literal: Right and wrong cannot be decided.
translations.idiomatic: Neither reading can be proved correct.

sentences.zh: 上文「椒房、中式數等」，「中式」也無考。

translations.literal: Above, "Chamber of Pepper and Central-style and other grades," "Central-style" also has no attestation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, among "Pepper Chamber, Central-style, and similar ranks," "Central-style" is likewise unattested.

sentences.zh: 桓帝立乃葬焉 諸本「桓」作「和」，殿本作「昭」，北史卷一三、御覽卷一三九

translations.literal: When Emperor Huan was installed, she was buried. In all editions "Huan" is written "He"; the Dian edition has "Zhao"; Beishi juan 13 and Yulan juan 139
translations.idiomatic: She was buried when Emperor Huan took the throne. Every edition writes "Huan" as "He"; Dian has "Zhao"; Beishi juan 13 and Yulan juan 139

作「桓」。

translations.idiomatic: have "Huan."

sentences.zh: 按和帝是遠祖，顯誤。

translations.literal: Comment: Emperor He was a remote ancestor—clearly an error.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Emperor He belongs to a distant generation; the reading is plainly wrong.

sentences.zh: 本書卷一序紀，稱昭帝二年「葬文帝及皇后封氏」。

translations.literal: This book, juan 1, Annals and Chronology, says in Zhao year 2, "Buried Emperor Wen and Empress Feng."
translations.idiomatic: Juan 1 of this work (Annals) records that in Zhao year 2 "Emperor Wen and Empress Feng were buried."

sentences.zh: 當時昭帝祿官和文帝沙漠汗之子桓帝猗㐌、穆帝猗盧分國為三部，各統其一，昭帝即位之二年也即是桓帝即位之二年。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Zhao had succeeded; Emperor He Yizhi and Emperor Mu Yilu, sons of Emperor Wen Shamo Khan, had divided the realm into three parts, each ruling one; Zhao's second year was also He's second year as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had just succeeded; He Yizhi and Mu Yilu, sons of Wen Shamo Khan, had split the state in three, each holding a third; Zhao’s second regnal year was also He’s second.

sentences.zh: 桓帝乃封氏子，故傳稱他即位葬母，今從北史、御覽改。

translations.literal: He was Empress Feng's son; the biography says he buried his mother upon his accession—now emended according to Beishi and Yulan.
translations.idiomatic: He was Feng’s son, so the account of burying his mother at enthronement fits; Beishi and Yulan are followed.

sentences.zh: 桓帝皇后祁氏 北史卷一三、御覽

translations.literal: Empress Qi of Emperor Huan: Beishi juan 13, Yulan
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qi, consort of Emperor Huan: Beishi juan 13, Yulan

translations.literal: Therefore Xian did not have them pursued urgently. Beishi reads "Therefore Xian had them not pursued urgently."
translations.idiomatic: Hence Xian did not order a hot pursuit. Beishi: "Hence Xian had them not pursued urgently."

sentences.zh: 按「顯使」指上文所云劉顯派來謀害拓跋珪之使，這裏「不使」二字當是誤倒。

translations.literal: Comment: "Xian's envoys" refers to the envoys Liu Xian sent above to plot against Tuoba Gui; here the two characters "did not have" are probably transposed.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "Xian's envoys" means the agents Liu Xian sent to kill Tuoba Gui; "bu shi" (did not have) here is likely a transposition.

translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother Meng was enfeoffed as Lady of Piaoyang. Yulan

translations.idiomatic: read "Li" for "Piao" (Piaoyang)—likely the right form.

sentences.zh: 高祖時 諸本「高祖」作「高宗」。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's time. In all editions "Gaozu" is written "Gaozong."
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu. All editions write "Gaozong" for "Gaozu."

sentences.zh: 按事見卷一０八之一禮志一太和十九年六月，「宗」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Comment: The matter appears in juan 108.1, Rites Treatise 1, sixth month of Taihe year 19; the character "zong" is corrupt—now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note: The event is in Rites Treatise 1 (juan 108.1), sixth month, Taihe year 19; "zong" is a slip for "zu," corrected here.

sentences.zh: 西城郡公 卷八三外戚馮熙傳作「遼西郡公」，墓誌集釋元悅妃馮季華墓誌

translations.idiomatic: Duke of Xicheng commandery. Juan 83 (External Kin, Feng Xi) has "Duke of Liaoxi"; the epitaph of Yuan Yue's wife Feng Jihua in Collected Explanations of Epitaphs

translations.idiomatic: styles the grandfather Lang "Duke of Xi commandery."

sentences.zh: 按朗與其兄崇於北燕未亡時，先降魏，崇封遼西王，事見卷九七馮跋傳。

translations.literal: Comment: Lang and his elder brother Chong surrendered to Wei before Northern Yan fell; Chong was enfeoffed Prince of Liaoxi—see juan 97, Biography of Feng Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Lang and his brother Chong defected to Wei before Northern Yan perished; Chong became Prince of Liaoxi (juan 97, Feng Ba).

sentences.zh: 崇既封遼西，朗似不得封遼西公。

translations.literal: Since Chong was enfeoffed Liaoxi, Lang could hardly be enfeoffed Duke of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: With Chong as Prince of Liaoxi, Lang could scarcely receive the same territory as a duke.

sentences.zh: 地形志不載「西城郡」或「西郡」。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Geography does not list "Xicheng commandery" or "Xi commandery."
translations.idiomatic: Neither Xicheng nor Xi commandery appears in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 然隋書卷二九地理志上張掖郡山丹條稱後魏「又有西郡」。

translations.literal: Yet Suishu juan 29, Treatise on Geography, Shandan entry under Zhangye commandery, says Later Wei "also had Xi commandery."
translations.idiomatic: Suishu juan 29 (Geography), Zhangye—Shandan, however, notes that Later Wei "also maintained Xi commandery."

sentences.zh: 疑作「西郡」是。

translations.idiomatic: "Xi commandery" is probably meant.

translations.literal: Comment: Reading "jie qi sheng bu" is unintelligible.

sentences.zh: 「省其信不」，是說幽后又派心腹雙蒙去省察所遣閹人是否可信。

translations.literal: "Sheng qi xin bu" means the Youhou Empress again sent her trusted follower Shuang Meng to inspect whether the eunuchs she dispatched were trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase means the Youhou Empress sent her confidant Shuang Meng to check whether the eunuchs she had dispatched were reliable.

sentences.zh: 如御覽，則意謂所遣閹人和雙蒙都是幽后信任的人。

translations.literal: As in Yulan, the sense is that both the dispatched eunuchs and Shuang Meng were men the Youhou Empress trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Yulan’s reading implies that the eunuchs and Shuang Meng alike were people she trusted.

sentences.zh: 意義不同，但都可通。

translations.literal: The meanings differ, but both are intelligible.
translations.idiomatic: The senses diverge, yet each construal is defensible.
